cases.why: Absent means false. Every course written before this key existed says exactly this.

cases.name: the key and its value on different lines
cases.why: THE ROW THIS TABLE EXISTS FOR. Reachable by a hand edit or a reformatter; no writer in the product produces it. Before the fix, this deployed.

cases.name: tabs and extra spaces around the colon
Windows line endings
cases.why: The same file written on the other platform. A carriage return is whitespace in all three dialects.

cases.name: a byte-order mark at the head of the file
cases.why: The launchers' grep never noticed a BOM. The Python did, and refused to parse the whole file - so it read as an ordinary course. Closed by opening the file as utf-8-sig, which costs nothing.

cases.name: the value in capitals
cases.why: Not valid JSON, so the apps cannot open this course at all and refusing costs a teacher nothing they could have used. Somebody hand-edited it meaning true.

cases.name: the value as a string
cases.why: CANNOT TELL. Somebody plainly meant the marker and wrote the value wrong. The app reads a real JSON boolean and nothing else, so it shows an ordinary course; the launchers refuse, which publishes nothing and freezes nothing. Refusing costs a teacher one puzzled moment on a course they hand-edited.

cases.name: the value as the number 1
cases.why: THE ROW THE APP WAS ADDED FOR. It used to read TRUE here - NSNumber bridges to Bool for 0 and 1 - so the app froze and locked a course every launcher then deployed. The app is strict now and the launchers say 'cannot tell'.

cases.name: the value as the number 1.0
cases.why: The same bridge, measured: 1.0 read as true as well.

cases.name: the value as the number 0
cases.why: Cannot tell, and deliberately NOT read as false: a zero is as much a hand-edit as a one, and guessing which way somebody meant it is the thing this rule refuses to do.

cases.name: the key written with unicode escapes ALL the way
cases.why: THE ROW THE ESCAPED-KEY RULE WAS ADDED FOR. Measured before it: the app decoded the escape, called it a reference course and LOCKED it, while the real deploy.sh walked straight past and published from --to-folder. A text reader cannot see this key at all, so the rule is about the ESCAPE rather than about the marker: any object key carrying a backslash-u escape reads as 'cannot tell'.

cases.name: an accented course NAME, as json.dump writes it
cases.why: The row that keeps the rule above honest. Python's json.dump escapes non-ASCII in VALUES by default, so accents and every emojis value carry backslash-u legitimately - refusing on those would refuse real courses. Proven against the four real previous-generation configs, all 38 example-content payloads and the app's own writer.

cases.name: a value that ends in an escaped quote and a colon
cases.why: The adversarial shape the escaped-key rule has to survive: a VALUE carrying both an escape and a colon. The [{,] anchor is what saves it - a key follows an opening brace or a comma, and this token follows a colon.

cases.name: a key that merely ENDS in the marker's tail
cases.why: The one shape refused with the REFERENCE-COURSE sentence rather than 'cannot tell', because the widened pattern is `"[^"]*ept_for_reference"` and this key ends in that tail. No such key exists in the product; the row is here so the surface is written down rather than discovered.

cases.name: the key written with unicode escapes
cases.why: All four agree it IS a reference course. JSON resolves the escape, so the app and the parsed half of the Python see the real key - and the TEXT pattern is written `"[^"]*ept_for_reference"` for exactly this: no ordinary key ends in those characters, so widening it costs nothing and catches every partially-escaped spelling.

cases.name: the key in capitals
cases.why: JSON keys are case-sensitive, so this is NOT the marker and every reader agrees it is an ordinary course. It is in the table because deploy.ps1's -match was case-INSENSITIVE and refused it, which would have stranded a Windows teacher with a live course whose Deploy button could never work. -cmatch, and the value's case spelled out instead.

cases.name: the settings file is a FOLDER
cases.why: Not a settings file at all, so not this check's business - the course-folder check answers it. In the table because PowerShell's Test-Path matches containers too, so deploy.ps1 refused it while the other three allowed it. -PathType Leaf.

cases.name: malformed JSON carrying the marker
cases.why: The app cannot open the course at all; the three text readers refuse the deploy. Nothing is frozen and nothing is published.

cases.name: malformed JSON with no marker
cases.why: The one place this errs toward allowing, deliberately: a course nobody can open must not become undeployable by accident.

cases.name: an empty settings file
no settings file at all
cases.why: Not this check's business. The launcher's own course-folder check answers it, in its own words.

cases.name: a settings file that cannot be read
cases.why: FAIL CLOSED. 'Cannot tell' is not 'no'. The launchers say so in a sentence of their own; the Python is asked the same question through cannot_tell(), so deploy.py run directly gives the same answer.

cases.name: the marker's text inside a course NAME
cases.why: MEASURED, and it turned out better than expected. A text rule looked as if it must mistake this for the real key - but JSON ESCAPES the quotes inside a string value, so what is actually in the file is \"kept_for_reference\", with backslashes, and none of the three patterns match it. The escaping is what tells a value from a key, for free, in all three dialects. The row is kept because the reasoning is not obvious and somebody will otherwise re-derive it as a hazard.

cases.name: the key nested inside another object
cases.why: Same reason. Refusing a course whose settings carry that text somewhere odd is the cheap direction.

refusal.sentence: {course} is kept for reference, so it is never deployed. Deploy the course you are teaching instead.
refusal.rule: Every door a deploy can start at refuses a reference course, with this sentence, BEFORE anything is stopped, built or uploaded. {course} is the code a TEACHER reads. The sentence says what the course is and names the way out - the course being taught - and it deliberately does NOT tell the teacher to copy anything. That stayed decided when Plantoir gained 'Copy a Page from This Course...' in the same release (issue #207): this is a refusal about DEPLOYING, and a refusal that advertises an unrelated feature is one a teacher has to read twice. The menu item is on the course's own row, where they will meet it.
refusal.doesNotDependOnTheLock: The refusal is gated on the MARKER alone and never on whether the files happen to be locked. An entirely unlocked reference course - one restored from a backup, or one whose folder has been on a second Mac - is refused at every door just the same. Both suites pin it. If the two were ever coupled, unlocking a course would make it deployable, and a deploy that reports success is the worst direction this feature can fail in.
refusal.gateByDirection: Refuse what would START a deploy; never refuse what STOPS one. Cancelling a scheduled deploy is always allowed, on every surface, however the course is marked - a course marked by hand while an alarm was already set must still be able to have that alarm turned off from the app. Whatever writes the marker cancels the course's scheduled deploys in the same act, and so does the pass that meets a reference course when the working folder is read.
refusal.failClosedInTheShell: The host-side check in deploy.sh and deploy.ps1 reads course_config.json in PLAIN SHELL - no host python3, which that path does not otherwise need on a product whose first-run promise is 'no Homebrew, no admin rights'. It fails CLOSED: a settings file that is there and cannot be read refuses, saying so. A settings file that is ABSENT is not this check's business - the launcher's own 'course folder not found' answers that - and a malformed one reads as NOT a reference course in the shared Python, because a course nobody can open must not become undeployable by accident.
refusal.whyNotANewExitCode: deploy.sh states its own invariant: exit 3 means 'a question nobody was there to answer' and nothing else, and every other exit is 0 or 1. A fourth code would have to be read by the scheduled wrapper, by ScheduledPublishOutcome and by the Windows twin before it meant anything. Exit 1, matched on OUTPUT by an app-rules.json -> failureExplanations case, which is how every other launcher failure already becomes a sentence.

doors.alsoCaughtBy: the button is not drawn at all on a reference course

doors.door: the local assistant's deploy_section, window branch
doors.chokepoint: AssistToolRunner.deploySection, before the preview is stopped
doors.why: Placed before the stop, not after: a refusal any later kills a preview the teacher was reading, for nothing.

doors.door: the local assistant's deploy_section, headless branch
the deploy approval card's Go button
doors.why: Closed by construction as well: the local assistant is never offered on a reference course, and a window request naming one is refused, so the card cannot be reached with one in hand.
Refused whatever time was asked for, before 'that time has already passed'.

doors.door: a scheduled deploy already on disk, firing at its moment
doors.why: The alarm was written before the course was marked. It is also cancelled when the folder is next read, but the Mac may not have been opened since - so the launcher has to refuse on its own.
Publishes nothing, but it would DESCRIBE a deploy that cannot happen - which teaches a session to try.

doors.door: ./deploy.sh <CODE> <N> by hand, to a web host

doors.chokepoint: deploy.sh's host-side check, and ONLY that
doors.why: THE TRAP. The folder publish is done with rsync on the HOST and exits 0 before the container is ever started, so deploy.py is never entered on this path. A refusal written only in the shared Python leaves this door wide open. Same shape as the live-reload defect of 2026-09-05, which is why verify.sh greps both launchers for it.
Windows' own. Its folder branch never enters the container either.
Before the 'section directory not found' check, so a course with no build yet is still told the real reason.
A harness rather than a door, and it is where the refusal is proved against the REAL launcher rather than a unit test.

toolsStillAllowed.why: A reference course may be previewed - that is how a teacher reads last year's pages with their images and links. It writes into the build tree, never into the course.

It reads the course and writes a zip into courses/_backups/, outside the course folder. The moment before risky editing is exactly when a copy is wanted, and a restored backup is still a reference course because the marker travels in the config.
Gate by DIRECTION: this is the act that STOPS a deploy. Refusing it would strand an alarm set before the course was marked, with no way to turn it off from the app.

refusal.aToolThatNamesNoCourse: One write tool declares no course argument at all - undo_last_change, which takes back whatever this conversation last did. It is gated by the course the PENDING CHANGE belongs to, read from the conversation's own history, rather than by an argument no client sends. A test asserts it is the ONLY non-readOnly tool without a course parameter, so a second one has to be given the same treatment deliberately instead of slipping past a gate that reads an argument and gives up when it is empty.
refusal.howTheWriteGateIsChosen: On the tool's OWN readOnly flag, never a hand-kept list of names - the same reasoning the window binding uses for gating on the schema. The three exemptions above are DATA rather than code, and a test asserts that the non-readOnly tools minus those three are exactly the set the gate refuses, so adding a tool fails the suite rather than opening a hole. And it is never gated on 'is this the course the session greeted': there is no such binding over MCP, and inventing one here to then except it would remove a capability that is the point of having a reference course at all.

interface.group: Reference Courses, folded into school-year sub-groups inside it. Newest year first, 'Other' last, and a group with nothing in it is NOT DRAWN - an empty '2023-24' is a row that teaches a teacher to stop reading the sidebar. Every group's fold state is remembered with the folder, the outer one and each year, the same way Archived and Backups already are.
interface.withheldNotRefused: Every act that would CHANGE a reference course is not offered at all - hidden, never greyed. A greyed control that can never become available is a standing invitation to wonder what is wrong, and this sidebar already follows that rule for Schedule/Cancel Deploy. The refusals stay underneath: a teacher meets the absence, and any other caller meets the refusal.
whatIsWithheld: Schedule Deploy... (Cancel Deploy at... is always offered - gate by direction)
Rename Course (the folder carries the year and course_code carries the real code; the two are allowed to disagree only here, and a rename would collapse them)
Remove Section N (removing the whole course stays)

the Course Settings FORM itself - a reference course's row opens a short read-only summary instead (the real code and name, its school year with the Set School Year... action beside it, its sections, and the two sentences). The form asked a never-deployed course to choose a deploy folder, greyed Save for ever with no explanation, and let every OTHER setting be saved - including the deploying settings whose emptiness is what makes an older Plantoir refuse the course
Course Settings' writes: the folder and unit-word renames, and Restore Section N...

the Site Health REPAIR button. The findings may still be reported; the button may not be drawn, because a repair returns no attempts on a frozen course and the zero-attempt branch reads as 'That is already put right. Nothing needed changing.' - about a folder that is really missing

Rename from EVERY route, not just the context menu: the Edit menu item and the Return key both went through courseThatCanBeRenamed, which said yes, set a rename in motion on a row that draws no editing field, and left Return-to-rename dead for every other course in the window
Site Health repairs, which CREATE files inside the course - and would succeed, because the folders are deliberately left unlocked so the preview can work
Revise with Claude... and Revise with Codex...
Keep a Copy for Reference... (a copy of a frozen copy has no purpose a teacher would recognise)
interface.theReadOnlySummary: What a reference course's row opens instead of the settings form: the code a teacher reads and the course name; the school year, with the one action a frozen course still offers; the sections; the FOLDER name, which is the one place a folder name is the fact; and wording.neverDeployed, wording.pagesAreLocked and wording.obsidianOpensThemForReading. No fields, no Save, and no control that can never become available.
whatIsOffered: Preview - the whole point of keeping the course

Copy a Page from This Course... - ALLOWED, and offered on every course row. It only READS this course; what it writes goes into a course the teacher TEACHES, chosen inside the sheet, which is never a reference course. Copying a page out of last year is a large part of why the course was kept, and the copy arrives UNLOCKED (see frozen.copyingOut) and hidden from students. Issue #207
Open in Obsidian, with the calm note in front of it the first time
Back Up Now - it only READS the course, and a restored backup is still a reference course
Remove - unlocks first, same confirmation, same words
Set School Year... - the one thing a frozen course still lets a teacher change, and it is a label on the shelf rather than a page
interface.theCalmNote: Shown when the copy is made AND before the teacher opens the course in Obsidian - once per course, remembered. In FRONT of them rather than after, because what Obsidian shows somebody typing into a locked page could not be measured and silent loss is not ruled out. It claims no more than wording.pagesAreLocked says: not that the pages cannot be changed (the lock is per-Mac and a cloud folder strips it while files upload), and not that the teacher will be TOLD when an edit fails. No warning icon, no 'cannot', no 'error'.
interface.theLocalAssistant: Not offered on a reference course and told nothing about one. The menu item is not drawn; a window request naming one opens no window, which also closes the deploy approval card as a door by construction; and list_courses does not list them to the LOCAL client - which matters because 'what courses do i have?' is matched in code and its answer is shown to the teacher.
interface.theMCPSurface: The opposite, deliberately: reading a reference course is the point of keeping it. The session briefing (initialize.instructions) names each one, list_courses marks the kind and the year, and every write refuses. A course is ADDRESSED by its folder name; a bare course code resolves to the LIVE course exactly as before, and if there is no live one it REFUSES and names the candidates rather than guessing - the two deliberately show the same code, so a guess would look right every time.

wording.staysAsItIs: {course} is kept for reference, so it stays as it is.
wording.couldNotSetSchoolYear: {course}'s school year could not be saved. Try again in a moment.
wording.cannotTellHeadline: Plantoir cannot tell whether {course} is kept for reference
wording.cannotTellBecauseUnreadable: its settings file could not be read
wording.cannotTellBecauseOddValue: its settings say something other than true or false
wording.pagesAreLocked: Plantoir keeps this course's pages locked, so they stay as they were.
wording.obsidianOpensThemForReading: Obsidian opens them for reading. If you switch a page to editing and type, Obsidian will say it couldn’t save, and the page stays as it was.
wording.neverDeployed: {course} is kept for reference. Preview it to read its pages; it is never deployed.
wording.copyAlreadyBeingMade: A copy called {folder} is already being made in another window, or in another copy of Plantoir.
wording.copyIsASnapshot: This records {course} as it is today. You can keep teaching it as usual — nothing here changes. To take a fresher copy later, delete this one first, then copy again.
wording.keepACopyLeavesAddOnsBehind: The copy is made without {course}'s Obsidian add-ons and their settings, so nothing in them can publish it. {course} keeps them.
wording.codeAlreadyInThatYear: You already have a {code} kept for reference from {year}. Choose a different school year.
wording.codeAlreadyWithNoYear: You already have a {code} kept for reference with no school year. Choose a school year for this one.
wording.rule: {course} is the code a TEACHER reads - ICS3U, never the folder name. The register is calm: a teacher who kept a course for reference asked for this, so being told about it reads as a fact rather than a warning. No 'cannot', no 'error', no icon, and never a word about how it is done. Said by the app when an act that would change the course is not available; the sentence does NOT tell the teacher to copy anything. Plantoir DOES copy pages between courses since issue #207 - 'Copy a Page from This Course...', on this course's own row - and the sentence still does not mention it: it is a refusal about changing THIS course, and naming a different feature inside it is a non-sequitur. A page a teacher takes out BY HAND in Finder still arrives locked; the sentence that said so ("A file you copy out of it stays locked until you untick Locked in Get Info.") was RETIRED by Russell on 2026-09-22 - a hand copy is unlikely now that the copy feature exists and unlocks what it copies, and 'Get Info' without 'Finder' told a teacher nothing. If a sentence about the Finder ever returns, it names the Finder.
wording.machineryCheck: No 'lock flag', 'immutable', 'permission', 'chflags', 'script' or 'container' in any sentence here. 'Locked' on its own is allowed: it is the word Finder and Get Info already use, and it is what a teacher sees on the file.
wording.theCannotTellSentence: Said by the LAUNCHERS only, as 'cannotTellHeadline - <one of the two reasons>. Nothing was published.' Both launchers carry it as a constant and a test compares them against these keys, the same arrangement refusal.sentence has. app-rules.json -> failureExplanations turns it back into the teacher's sentence when a deploy set to happen on its own hits it, which is the population it exists for: that one runs with the app closed, and the app reads such a course as ORDINARY, so the teacher can schedule it and only the launcher will refuse.
wording.whyTheLaunchersStillSayPublished: 'Nothing was published.' is the launchers' own long-standing house sentence - five times in each of them on dev, asserted by two shared Python tests - and it is deliberately NOT changed to 'deployed' here. Russell's decision (r) governs the APP's sentences and every new key name, and every sentence in this block follows it; one launcher run saying both words for the same act would be worse than one word that is old. A launcher vocabulary sweep is its own piece of work.

frozen.theWalk: Every content FILE, at every depth. skipDescendants() is for a never-locked FOLDER and must never be called for a never-locked FILE: the enumerator applies the skip to the next directory it has not descended into, so the folder AFTER course_config.json - which every course has at its top level - was never walked and never locked. Measured on a real course: 842 of 934 files walked, 27 real pages left editable, and WHICH folder was lost moved between passes with readdir order, so the course came out mostly locked and never entirely locked. Counting what the pass WALKED against what is locked afterwards does NOT catch this - a walk that skips a folder never counts that folder, so the two numbers agree and the fault reports success (it did: nine pages editable, everything-is-locked true). What catches it is an independent CENSUS taken after the pass: a plain full listing of the course with no skip logic at all, each regular file classified by the never-locked rule alone, and the number that SHOULD be locked compared with the number whose flag says locked. A mismatch is put on the trail with both numbers, and the sentence that says the pages are kept locked is not shown. Measured with the old fault put back: 13 of 16.
frozen.offTheMainActor: The walk runs off the caller's actor - measured at ~24 ms with nothing to do and ~80 ms for a full pass on 1,220 files, which is not a teacher's click to wait for after every sheet. On the mac that takes @concurrent, not merely `nonisolated async`: the target builds with SWIFT_APPROACHABLE_CONCURRENCY, under which a nonisolated async function runs on its CALLER's actor - so the obvious spelling would have kept every stat on the main actor while reading as though it did not. A test asserts the work is not on the main thread rather than trusting the annotation. No DispatchQueue and no sleeps anywhere.
frozen.rule: The pages of a reference course are LOCKED ON DISK - Finder's Locked, the user-immutable flag - on every content FILE and on no directory. Plantoir itself offers nothing that changes a page, a setting or the shape of the course.
frozen.mechanism: chflags uchg, and only that. Modes are left exactly as they are.
frozen.whyNotPermissions: Measured twice over. (1) chmod a-w does not stop a RENAME-OVER, which is how every serious editor saves: the measurement replaced a page's contents at exit 0, and rm -f deleted it. The immutable flag refuses both, and refuses a rename and a delete as well. (2) Mode 444 BREAKS THE PREVIEW BUILD, which is the finding that settled it: build_site.py copies each page into the build tree with shutil.copy2 (mode and flags travel), then rewrites the copy's frontmatter, which is where draft: true becomes publish: false. The build tree in THAT measurement was a host bind mount, where the container's root does NOT get its usual permission override - measured inside the real image - so the rewrite fails with one warning per page, the copy keeps draft: true and gains no publish key, and the Explorer publishes anything that does not say publish: false. Every page the teacher had HIDDEN would have appeared in the preview of their frozen course. With the flag alone and the mode left at 644, the same build writes publish: false correctly AND the source is still refused even to container root. WHERE THE MAC ACTUALLY BUILDS, said so that reason is not read as a description of the shipping pipeline: toolchain_paths.WORK_DIR, the container's own /tmp/quartz-builds, with only public/ synced out - so on the mac the rewrite happens on container-local storage where root CAN write a 444 file, and the must-fail does not reproduce through the launcher. Reason (1), that chmod a-w does not stop a rename-over, carries the decision on its own and is untouched by this. ON WINDOWS THE FAULT IS REACHABLE: preview.ps1 and deploy.ps1 point PLANTOIR_WORK_DIR at a HOST folder under %LOCALAPPDATA% and build natively rather than as root, so a read-only attribute travels into the build tree, the frontmatter rewrite would fail, and a page the teacher HID would be published. Whatever mechanism Windows chooses, run a real build of a locked course and check that a hidden page is still hidden.
frozen.whyNotDirectories: Measured: with the course folder locked, creating the .merged_output symlink inside it fails - and BuildOutputLocation has to create that link on every reload, as do the launchers before every build. Locking the folders would kill the preview a reference course exists to give.

neverLocked.name: course_config.json
neverLocked.why: The school year can be changed later, and the build's own preflight rewrites this file whenever a folder list changes.

neverLocked.name: course_config.backup.json
neverLocked.why: Written beside it by that same preflight, with shutil.copy2, which raises on a locked destination.

neverLocked.name: course_config.json.tmp
neverLocked.why: The other half of that atomic write - it exists only between the open() and the os.replace(). A build interrupted between the two leaves it on disk, and a LOCKED one would then fail every later preflight twice over: the write into it and the cleanup that removes it. That course's settings could never be reconciled again. Anything ending .tmp is left alone for the same reason, whatever its name.

neverLocked.name: .obsidian
neverLocked.why: Obsidian writes workspace.json the moment a vault is opened, and opening the course in Obsidian is the whole point of keeping it. The folder and everything under it - themes, snippets, the workspace, and the add-ons of a course kept before #255 - are outside the lock.

neverLocked.name: .merged_output
neverLocked.why: The built website. A symlink out of the folder, rebuilt rather than kept, and never locked through the link.

neverLocked.name: .DS_Store
neverLocked.why: Finder's own bookkeeping. Nothing a teacher wrote.

whatPlantoirStillWrites.why: Created or repaired on every read of the folder, and by the launchers before every build. Inside the course folder, which is why the directories stay unlocked.
Folder and file discovery reconciles the lists whenever the teacher's folders and the config disagree. Bookkeeping about what is there, not a change to a page.
On open. Outside the lock deliberately.

whatPlantoirStillWrites.what: an exclusion note inside a folder's index.md
whatPlantoirStillWrites.why: The one writer that CAN meet a locked file. It returns without writing when the note already matches, and it catches the write failure, so on a reference course it is a warning line at worst - not a failed build. Named here so neither platform reads it as a bug.

removing.aWholeCourse: Allowed, and it unlocks first. Measured: FileManager.removeItem and rm -rf both refuse a locked tree. The unlock happens after the scheduled-deploy cancel and before the archive, so the one thing that can stop a removal is still the cancel. The teacher is told nothing about the lock - a delete confirmation that mentioned it would be the app talking about its own plumbing.
removing.oneSection: REFUSED, with wording.staysAsItIs. Removing a section changes the course, so 'frozen' already requires it. The sidebar does not offer the item; the refusal exists so no other caller can get past it, and so what a teacher reads is a sentence rather than the file system's own words about an operation not being permitted.
removing.theOnlySection: The sidebar turns that into removing the whole COURSE, so it takes the unlock-then-remove path above.

frozen.restoring: A zip round trip carries the MODE and loses the flag - measured - so a restored reference course arrives thawed. The marker travels in the config, so the marker is what puts the lock back: every restore path unlocks what it is about to write over and locks again afterwards, asked of the config as it is AFTER the restore. A backup made before the course was kept for reference therefore restores a course that is not one, which is right.
frozen.copyingOut: The flag TRAVELS. FileManager.copyItem, cp -p, ditto and shutil.copy2 all carry it; only a plain cp -R or a zip round trip loses it. So anything copied out of a reference course arrives locked unless it is cleared, and a page a teacher cannot edit with no explanation reads as 'the app is broken'. Whatever copies pages between courses must clear it, and since issue #207 something does: 'Copy a Page from This Course...' clears the flag on every page it writes and every picture it copies, proved by a must-fail test that locks the source first.
frozen.inObsidian: MEASURED by Russell on 2026-09-23, the one thing the run could not drive: typing into a locked page makes Obsidian show a notice that the file could not be saved (its own wording, ending with advice to make a backup - nothing is lost), and the page stays as it was. So the refusal is loud, not silent. On top of that, a reference course is made with Obsidian's reading view as the vault's default (`defaultViewMode: preview` in .obsidian/app.json - the key and its values read out of Obsidian's own bundle; Obsidian has no read-only mode for a vault), so pages open rendered rather than ready to edit and the ordinary path never meets the refusal. .obsidian is never locked, which is why this can be written after the lock is on. Best effort: a settings file Obsidian could not read is left alone, and the lock, not this, is what keeps the pages. Windows: write the same key into the same file when a reference course is made.
frozen.reAsserted: The lock is asserted, VERIFIED by reading the flag back, and re-asserted. Setting it without checking is not enough: in a cloud-synced folder the file provider models the locked bit itself, does not store it, and clears it locally about a second after an upload starts - no error, no log line. So the lock is per-Mac, a folder that has been on a second Mac comes back unlocked, and the re-assertion points are when the folder is read and when the teacher acts on the course. Files that did not take are left for the next pass and COUNTED on the trail. Never a timer and never a sleep: a delay chosen to let something settle is a guess that stops working on a slower machine.
frozen.honestLimits: Stated plainly in the documentation and NEVER in the GUI. With the directories unlocked a new file can still be ADDED to one. Anybody who means to can clear the flag. The lock is per-Mac, and an edit arriving from another device is not blocked by it. What the lock does stop is every ordinary edit, save, rename and delete of the material that is there, which is what a teacher will meet - it is a statement of intent, not a security boundary. The refusal to deploy does NOT depend on it in any way: an entirely unlocked reference course is refused at every door just the same.

rejected.what: A second display_code key
rejected.why: A third spelling of one fact, and it would leave the site builder writing ICS3U-2025 into the site title and social card of a course whose preview the teacher is reading.

rejected.what: Renaming Course.code to folderName
rejected.why: 273 call sites across 55 files for a rename that buys clarity and no behaviour, inside a piece whose dangerous half is the refusal.

rejected.what: A lower-case folder suffix (ICS3U-examples)
rejected.why: The launchers put their course argument through tr '[:lower:]' '[:upper:]' before building courses/<CODE>, so the folder would simply not be found. Every proposed folder name is upper case, and a test pins that it survives being normalised again.

rejected.what: A free-text label beside the code instead of a school year
rejected.why: Russell's decision: rows are told apart by school year. A typed label is a second naming system to validate, and two teachers' labels for the same thing would not sort.

rejected.what: A reference/ sibling folder beside courses/
rejected.why: Everything that finds a course walks courses/ — discovery, the launchers, the build output link, the backups list. A second home would be a second answer to 'where are the courses', and the marker gives the same separation for one key.

obsidianAddOns.note: #255 (2026-09-25). EVERY route that makes a reference course - Keep a Copy for Reference..., and Import Courses for Reference... reading a modern working folder, the older folder-per-class layout (importing.olderLayout) or the 2024-25 website-folder-per-class layout (importing.quartzCheckoutLayout) - leaves the same three entries of the course's .obsidian behind and brings the rest. Before #255 only the two older layouts did; a modern import and Keep a Copy brought plugins/ and community-plugins.json across whole.
obsidianAddOns.rule: Anchored at the course's OWN top-level .obsidian (content/.obsidian in the 2024-25 layout) and compared as a PATH, never matched as a name: a teacher's own folder of pages called plugins, anywhere in the course, comes across. Each entry is skipped WITHOUT being looked inside - before it is so much as lstat-ed - so nothing inside an add-on can refuse a course (an unreadable folder in there is not an unreadable folder of the course). On the two MODERN routes a .obsidian that is itself a LINK does not come at all: it is never copied as a link, because the reference course would then be reading - and the reading-view default WRITING into - the live settings it points at. The older layout already leaves every link out, and the 2024-25 layout judges every link at the top of content/ on its own, so neither needs that half. Keep a Copy of a LIVE course follows the same rule (Russell, 2026-09-25): the copy is never published, so an add-on in it is only ever a way to publish it outside the refusals, and the course being taught keeps its add-ons untouched.

leftBehindInsideObsidian.why: Every community add-on: its code and its settings. An add-on runs code with network access, and a publishing add-on keeps its credential in its own data.json - every real 2023-24 class folder carries digitalgarden/data.json with a non-empty githubToken (importing.olderLayout.placement.whyTheAddOnsStayBehind). Copied, the credential lands in the working folder and in every backup and archive zip, and once Obsidian trusts the vault's add-ons it is a publish command outside all fifteen of Plantoir's refusals.
The list of add-ons Obsidian switches on. Nothing to switch on without plugins/, and a list naming an add-on that is not there is only clutter.

Core Obsidian Publish's connection to a LIVE site - {siteId, host, included, excluded}. MEASURED in Obsidian 1.13.6's own bundle: a core add-on's loadData is vault.readConfigJson(id), which reads <configDir>/<id>.json. With the teacher signed in to Obsidian, a copied publish.json is one click from publishing the reference course over the site it came from. Core Sync is NOT here: its remote is kept in Obsidian's own storage keyed by the vault (IndexedDB '<appId>-sync', measured in the same bundle), so a copied folder carries nothing of it. 0 publish.json files in Russell's 2023-24 folders and 0 in the 2025-26 backup.

kept.why: Editor and appearance settings, the teacher's own; ReferenceReadingView writes defaultViewMode here after the copy.
How the vault looks. CSS cannot publish anything, and a theme is CSS.
Which of Obsidian's own features are on. It holds switches ("sync": true, "publish": false in Russell's four), never an account or a site - the site lives in publish.json, left behind above.

Every path in workspace.json is vault-relative (importing.leftBehind.kept). The conflicted copies - 63 of them in MPM2DE's .obsidian, 'workspace (<name>'s conflicted copy <date>).json' - are a sync provider's clutter, not a danger, and matching them would mean matching every provider's naming in every language. They come (Russell, 2026-09-25).
Folder state and preferences. Nothing in them runs code or reaches a website.

obsidianAddOns.hasAddOnsWhen: The sheets say it, and the modern trail lines name it, ONLY when there is something: plugins/ holds at least one entry whose name does not start with '.', or plugins/ is itself a link, or plugins/ is a folder that could not be listed, or .obsidian is itself a link, or publish.json is there. An empty plugins/ and a community-plugins.json of [] - Russell's own ICS3U, measured - say NOTHING: telling a teacher their add-ons were left behind when they had none is false. Add-ons are named by FOLDER name only; nothing inside an add-on is ever opened, and nothing read from one is ever written down.
obsidianAddOns.whereItIsSaid: Import sheet, under the list and in the summary: wording.addOnsAreLeftBehind when a MODERN course in the list has add-ons - true of every route, so it is said INSTEAD of wording.olderLayoutAddOnsAreLeftBehind, which beside a modern course with an add-on would read as if that one's add-ons came; otherwise the older sentence for any older-layout class, as before; otherwise nothing. Keep a Copy sheet, in the calm note before the copy is made: referenceCourses.wording.keepACopyLeavesAddOnsBehind, only when the live course has add-ons. The trail: 'course kept for reference' and, for a modern course, 'course imported for reference' end with what was left behind when there was anything, and are byte-identical to before when there was not. The older layouts keep counting theirs on their own second line, which is why the shared import line adds nothing for them.
obsidianAddOns.treeEntries: The grammar of importing.olderLayout.treeEntries: a plain string is a file (content 'something'), except a path ending course_config.json, which is written as settings naming the folder as its course_code with section_numbers [1]; one ending '/' is an empty folder; {"file": path, "text": "..."} is a file with that content; {"link": path, "to": "<path in the tree>"} is a link to that path. Each case is built at a root, and its course is root/<course>. On Windows a directory link can be a junction (a symlink needs Developer Mode); any reparse point must be treated as a link - never followed, never copied.

cases.name: a publishing add-on, with everything else Obsidian keeps beside it
a course Plantoir made: no add-ons, and nothing said
Russell's ICS3U as measured: an empty add-ons folder and an empty list
a teacher's own pages called plugins come: the rule is a place, not a name
the add-ons folder is a link: left behind, never followed, and said
a sync provider's conflicted copies of the workspace come along
the settings folder itself is a link: not copied, and the live settings are not written through it
the settings folder itself is a link and holds no app.json: not copied, and no settings file is made in the live folder
core Obsidian Publish connected to a live site: its setting stays behind

obsidianAddOns.howToRunACase: Build the tree, then make a reference course from root/<course> BOTH ways - Keep a Copy (the course as a live one) and a modern import (choosing root, a working folder holding courses/) - into a different working folder. Every expectAbsent path is not in the made course (not as a file, a folder or a link); every expectUnchanged path is byte-identical to its source; every expectNotALink path is not a link; the ENTIRE source tree, links' targets included, is byte-identical afterwards; what was found is expectFound; the sheet's note is said exactly when expectSaid. Two things are Swift-only because they are platform mechanics rather than data: a folder inside an add-on that nobody can read does not refuse the course on any of the four routes, and the sheet's size leaves the add-ons out.

knownLimits.why: The rule is anchored at the course's own top-level .obsidian, so a nested one (section1/.obsidian/plugins) comes across whole. MEASURED: the 2025-26 backup holds exactly four .obsidian folders, found case-insensitively and at any depth, all at a course's top; the 2023-24 class folders are routed through importing.olderLayout. None is met today.

knownLimits.what: Another spelling of the folder names
knownLimits.why: Compared exactly: .Obsidian/Plugins would come across although APFS would let Obsidian load it. The same measurement found only the lower-case spelling; matching case-insensitively was weighed and left for when a real folder needs it, because a rule that is exactly the file system's spelling is the one both platforms can run as data.
Obsidian can be told to keep a vault's settings in a folder other than .obsidian ('Override config folder'). Such a folder is copied as the teacher's own. Not met in any folder measured.

rejected.what: An allow-list of 'harmless' add-ons (Excalidraw, Dataview)
rejected.why: Any add-on runs arbitrary code with network access. Plantoir cannot judge third-party code, and the list would rot the day an add-on it named shipped an update.

rejected.what: Copying the add-ons but stripping credentials from data.json
rejected.why: Every add-on names its settings differently - githubToken is one of thousands - so which key is a credential cannot be known.

rejected.what: Copying plugins/ but not community-plugins.json, so the add-ons arrive switched off
rejected.why: The credential still lands in the folder and in every zip, and one toggle in Obsidian switches the add-on back on.

rejected.what: Walking the add-ons and filtering them out afterwards
rejected.why: The walk would still go inside plugins/, so an unreadable folder in an add-on would refuse the whole course for something never going to be copied. This is what the two older layouts did until #255; they skip now.

rejected.what: Adding plugins to the by-name list (importing.leftBehind.names)
rejected.why: That list matches at every depth, so it would drop a teacher's own folder of pages called plugins anywhere in the course (case 4).

rejected.what: A different rule for Keep a Copy of a live course
rejected.why: The copy is a reference course and is never published, whoever installed the add-on; the live course keeps its add-ons untouched. Russell, 2026-09-25.

rejected.what: Leaving the conflicted workspace copies behind
rejected.why: Clutter, not danger, and matching a sync provider's naming means matching every provider in every language. Russell, 2026-09-25: they come.

rejected.what: Leaving the modern route as it was because Plantoir-made courses carry no add-ons
rejected.why: True today, and exactly the quiet difference between routes that nobody chose: a teacher who installs one add-on in a live course would have it copied into every reference copy of it.

importing.note: The SECOND way a reference course is made: the teacher points at the folder they kept last year's classes in and ticks the courses they want. It is the same act as 'Keep a Copy for Reference…' with a different source, and it ends in the same code — cut loose from last year's websites, marked, filed under a school year, left with nowhere to deploy to, locked. Everything in the referenceCourses block above therefore applies to an imported course without exception: the same marker, the same neutralisation, the same fifteen refusals, the same lock.

theSourceIsNeverWritten.rule: The chosen folder is opened for reading only. Nothing inside it is created, renamed, removed or opened for writing, and that includes the build output, the site markers and the settings. Everything the import writes is inside the NEW folder in this working folder.
theSourceIsNeverWritten.why: It may be the teacher's only copy of last year. An import that failed costs an afternoon; an import that damaged the source costs the year. The neutralisation and the lock happen to the COPY, after it is made.

foldersAccepted.rule: Three shapes are accepted, and all three resolve to the same working folder: the folder itself (it holds a courses folder), the courses folder inside it, and ONE course folder (it holds course_config.json). A course is a folder inside courses/ that holds a course_config.json - nothing else is, which is what keeps _backups, .internal and any stray folder out without a list of names. Read by exact name, never by glob. When the chosen folder is none of these three, the OLDER folder-per-class layout is tried next (olderLayout below), then the 2024-25 website-folder-per-class layout (quartzCheckoutLayout below), and only when neither finds anything is the folder refused with noCoursesThere.
foldersAccepted.why: A teacher points at what they recognise rather than at what the app expects, and refusing a folder that plainly holds a course - because they went one level too deep - reads as the app being broken. Resolving upward costs nothing and the whole shelf is then offered, with the one they pointed at already ticked.
foldersAccepted.tickedWhenOpened: Everything, when a working folder or a courses folder was chosen: they pointed at last year and they mean last year. Only the one course, when a course folder was chosen: they were specific, and the others are offered rather than assumed.

cases.name: the old working folder
the courses folder itself
one course folder
cases.why: Resolved UPWARD: the whole shelf is offered, and only the one they pointed at is ticked.

cases.name: a folder with nothing of the kind in it
a courses folder holding only backups
cases.why: A folder of zips is not a course: a course is a folder holding course_config.json.

cases.name: the working folder this window already has open
cases.why: That is route 1's job, and the refusal says so by name rather than leaving the teacher to guess.

cases.name: a folder inside the one already open
cases.why: Copying a folder into itself is a folder inside itself, and the build output link would loop.

cases.name: a folder that HOLDS the one already open
cases.why: The other direction of the same fault, and the one that had a sentence and no case until 2026-09-20.

cases.name: a course folder that is not in a courses folder
cases.why: Resolving upward offers what is BESIDE the course, which is right inside a courses folder and wrong anywhere else: a course folder dragged onto the Desktop would otherwise offer every course-shaped folder on the Desktop, and name the home folder as the source. On its own instead.

leftBehind.rule: Composed from the lists that already exist rather than written out again: what an archive leaves behind, plus what a reference copy leaves behind, plus what only an import meets. A name in the list is skipped WITHOUT being looked inside, at any depth. The Obsidian add-ons are NOT on this list, because they are a place rather than a name: referenceCourses.obsidianAddOns. On this route a symlink is copied as a link and never followed - the only one a modern course holds is .merged_output, which is left behind by name anyway; changing that here was rejected (olderLayout.rejected). The older-layout route never copies a link at all: olderLayout.placement.whyNoLinkComesAcross.
leftBehind.why: On a folder made by an older Plantoir, .merged_output is a real directory holding last year's entire built website - measured at 1.9 GB per course against 489 MB of course, four fifths of what is on disk. Walking it to not copy it would cost more time than copying the course. On a folder made by a current Plantoir it is a symlink pointing out of the working folder, and following it would copy the built site back into the course it came from.

names.name: .merged_output
names.why: Last year's built website. Rebuilt on demand; a real directory in an old folder, a symlink in a new one, skipped either way.

names.name: .DS_Store
names.why: Finder's own bookkeeping. Nothing a teacher wrote.

names.name: course_config.backup.json
names.why: Yesterday's settings, left beside today's by the build's own bookkeeping.

names.name: course_config copy.json
names.why: A Finder duplicate, found in a real course in the measured folder. Not dangerous - the settings are read by exact name - but it is last year's clutter and a reference course should not arrive with it.

names.name: .Trashes
names.why: What a folder picks up from living on an external disk, which is exactly where an old working folder tends to be found.

alsoRemovedAfterTheCopy.why: Leases name processes on whichever machine wrote them, so a copied one names a process that was never doing anything here.

kept.why: The course may be opened in Obsidian, and Plantoir opens the course folder AS a vault. Without it the vault opens with first-run prompts, none of the teacher's appearance, and none of the folder state that makes last year's material navigable. 312 KB against a 489 MB course. Its workspace.json was MEASURED on a real imported course rather than assumed: every path in it is vault-relative (main/left/right/left-ribbon/active/lastOpenFiles), with no absolute path and no mention of the old folder, so it resolves inside the new course as it stands. Nothing needs stripping and nothing needs registering - the app opens a vault by path and registers nothing itself. Since #255 it comes WITHOUT its add-ons on this route too - plugins/, community-plugins.json and publish.json, the rule every route keeps (referenceCourses.obsidianAddOns) - and not at all when .obsidian is itself a link. Until then only the older folder-per-class layout left them behind.
Copied, then renamed aside by the same neutralisation route 1 uses. The file holds the site id and the admin address, which a teacher may still want.
A reference course is a faithful record of what students actually saw. The frontmatter of a page is NEVER rewritten on import - the build already reads the older draft: true/false correctly.

folderNameProduced.rule: The same rule route 1 uses, and the same function: CODE-YYYY in upper case, or CODE-REF when no school year was chosen, with -2 to -9 tried in turn when the name is taken. The course_code inside is left exactly as it was, so the teacher reads ICS4U while the folder is ICS4U-2025.

cases.why: The launchers upper-case their course argument before looking for the folder, so a lower-case folder is simply not found.

schoolYearProposed.rule: The school year most of the course's pages were last changed in, ties going to the NEWER year. A year outside the offered list proposes nothing and the teacher picks. It is a starting point the teacher changes, and nothing in the interface says how it was arrived at.
schoolYearProposed.why: The NEWEST page was measured and rejected: one page is exactly what gets touched by accident - opening last year's folder to look something up, or a sync putting a fresh date on one note. On the real folder, ICS4U's newest page is dated 2026-09-11, which proposes 2026-27, while 201 of its 287 pages were last changed in 2025-26, the year it was taught. The commonest year gets all four measured courses right; the newest page gets three.

nothingIsVisibleUntilItIsSafe.rule: A course is copied under a HIDDEN name inside courses/ - a folder whose name begins with a fixed prefix - and is marked, filed under its year, neutralised and locked THERE. The last act is a rename into its real name, which is atomic within one folder. Nothing under courses/ is ever a course that is not already a reference course. The same staging is used by BOTH ways one is made.
nothingIsVisibleUntilItIsSafe.why: Until 2026-09-20 the copy was made at its final name, so for the length of the copy the folder held last year's REAL site markers beside settings with no marker and no deploy_target - which reads as Netlify. Measured: a launcher run against that half-made folder does not refuse at all. A crash, a quit or a power cut in that window left an ordinary-looking live course in the sidebar with a working Deploy button aimed at last year's class site, and if the source was itself frozen the leftover could not even be deleted. The window was about two seconds for a file system that clones, and the WHOLE COPY on an external disk - which is the case the importer is written for.

hiddenFromWhat.why: It skips hidden entries. Pinned by a test rather than assumed.
The same. Pinned by a test.
The same. Pinned by a test.

They REFUSE a course argument beginning with a dot, before anything else, in all four of them. That refusal is the guard; until 2026-09-20 this line claimed the shape was impossible, and it was not - measured, deploy.sh uppercased the hidden name, the case-insensitive volume resolved it, and the run went straight past the reference gate because during the copy there is no marker yet to find. The app can never pass such a name (discovery skips hidden entries and a course code may not begin with a dot), but a person or another program can type one.

nothingIsVisibleUntilItIsSafe.sweptOnLoad: Leftovers are removed when a working folder is read - unlock first, because the lock is applied before the rename and a locked tree refuses to be removed - and ONE trail line says which courses they were going to be. Matched on the exact prefix and nothing else: a teacher's own dot-folder is never ours to take.
nothingIsVisibleUntilItIsSafe.aRunningImportIsLeftAlone: The import takes a LEASE naming its own process - <FOLDER>.import.<pid>.lease in courses/.internal/activity/, the NAME shape every work lease has, holding the four lines file-formats.json -> workLease describes (process id, process name, the moment it was taken, and when its owner started) - and the sweep skips any staging folder whose lease names a LIVE owner, removing the stale lease of one whose owner is gone. Who counts as alive is workLeases.liveness, the one reader every lease shares: another account's process is ALIVE (the system says it exists and is not ours to signal - until #245 that answer read as gone and the folder was swept), a process that has finished is gone, and a process id handed on to another process is gone, told by the name and the start time. Reading a working folder is not rare while an import runs: File > Reload Courses is offered with the sheet up, a second window on the same folder reads it, and an MCP session starts by reading it. Without the lease, one of those deletes the tree under a running copy - and after the lock and before the rename it would throw away a FINISHED reference course. Asked of a lease rather than of the folder's AGE on purpose: a threshold is a guessed duration, and the case that needs it most is the slow disk where the guess is wrong. KNOWN LIMIT: a lease that arrives by cloud sync from ANOTHER computer names a process id that means nothing on this one, so it reads as gone and that computer's half-made folder is swept here (and the sweep syncs back). The lease does not cover two computers sharing one synced working folder, and nothing here pretends it does.
nothingIsVisibleUntilItIsSafe.rejected: Staging OUTSIDE courses/ (the system temporary folder). It is a different volume, so the last step would be a copy rather than a rename - the whole window back again, and twice the bytes.

oneImportPerCourseAtATime.rule: Claiming a staging folder is ONE act, and only the claimer ever removes a staging folder. In order: (1) already claimed in THIS app - another window - is refused; (2) the claimer takes its own lease, THEN looks for another process's live lease, and one found is refused; (3) a leftover of that name, which nobody live owns, is cleared, and one that will not go means the import does not start; (4) the folder is made EXCLUSIVELY, and a folder already there means somebody slipped in, which is refused. Every answer but 'claimed' gives the claimer's lease back and removes nothing it did not put there. A refused course is reported with wording.alreadyBeingImported (Keep a Copy for Reference... with referenceCourses.wording.copyAlreadyBeingMade), a course that could not start with wording.leftoverInTheWay or the system's own sentence, and the other courses of the run carry on. The staging folder exists, empty, from the claim; nothing after it makes it again.
oneImportPerCourseAtATime.why: Two windows are ONE process with one process id, so a lease cannot tell them apart. Traced on the code before #245: window A checks (nobody), leases, and goes off to read the old folder; window B checks, reads A's lease as a live owner - its own id - so skips the leftover removal, leases the same file, and later fails to make the folder A already made; its catch then TIDIED AWAY the staging folder, which was A's half-made copy, and its release deleted the lease A still depended on. Keep a Copy for Reference... had the identical catch, and runs between the importer's suspension points, so it could do the same to an import of the same folder name in the same app. Across two processes the same create-failed-then-tidy path did it without the id coincidence.
oneImportPerCourseAtATime.whyLeaseThenCheck: Of two processes, the one that looks second always sees the first one's lease, so they can never both go on. At worst both step back and both say so - a refusal the teacher can simply retry, never a copy removed under somebody. Check-then-lease has a window where both see nobody.
oneImportPerCourseAtATime.claimKey: The in-app set is keyed by the courses folder's REAL path (links resolved, /private kept, the disk's own spelling of each name) plus the staging name in lower case, so two windows that reached one working folder by different spellings - a link, /private, another case on a case-insensitive disk - are still one claim.
oneImportPerCourseAtATime.residual: A Reload Courses in ANOTHER process that reads the folder in the moment between this claim's lease check and its removal of a leftover can still see no live lease on a folder about to be made. The import then fails and says so; it never leaves a half-made course visible and never touches the source. An OLDER copy of Plantoir (before #245) still checks, then leases, then makes the folder late, and its own tidy-up can still remove a newer copy's work - it cannot be taught otherwise from here.

another copy of Plantoir holds a live lease
another copy of Plantoir holds a live lease and its half-made folder is there - left alone
a leftover nobody owns is cleared, then the folder is made
a leftover that will not go: not started
somebody made the folder between the check and the create: refused, nothing removed
the folder could not be made for another reason: not started, and the system's sentence is the reason

oneImportPerCourseAtATime.howToRunACase: claimedInThisApp: put the key in the app's own set first. anotherLiveLease: write <FOLDER>.import.<pid>.lease naming a process that is alive and not this one (the mac suite uses pid 1, which is alive and another account's, with a body naming it launchd - a lease with no name line would be judged as Plantoir's, and launchd is not). leftover: 'removable' is a staging folder holding one file; 'cannotBeRemoved' is the same with the removal step made to fail. create: 'made' is the real create; 'alreadyThere' and 'failed' are the create step made to answer so. expect.leftover: 'removed' - the folder's file is gone; 'leftAlone' - it is still there; 'none' - there was none. leaseKept: whether the claimer's own lease is on disk afterwards. reason: which sentence the teacher is given, 'theCreateFailure' being the create step's own.
rejected: The second import WAITS for the first. A wait-and-poll is a guessed duration by another name, and it would end in a refusal anyway: once the first lands, the same code in the same school year is refused by the shelf rule. Refusing now, with a sentence, is the same end without a spinner.
Making the folder earlier WITHOUT the in-app set. A create cannot tell window A's folder from a crashed leftover, and the leftover removal before it is exactly what cleared A's work away.

A unique token in the lease NAME, to tell two windows apart. An older build parses the pid out of the name, fails on the token, skips the lease - and would SWEEP a live import, the exact hazard this is.

flock on the lease file. Nothing else reads a lock (older builds and Windows read names and pids), and working folders live on cloud-synced volumes where advisory locks are not something to bet a teacher's copy on.

oneCourseFailingDoesNotStopTheRest.rule: Each ticked course is imported on its own. One that cannot be - its code is already kept for reference under that school year, its folder could not be read, the disk filled - is reported for that course, by name, with what happened, and the run carries on to the next. Only the teacher pressing Stop ends a run early.
oneCourseFailingDoesNotStopTheRest.why: A folder of four courses where one has a problem must import three. An import that abandons everything at the first trouble makes the teacher work out which of the four it was, and do the other three again.
oneCourseFailingDoesNotStopTheRest.theSheetMarksTheROW: A course that cannot be filed - its code is already kept for reference under that school year - is marked BESIDE ITS OWN ROW and the others can still be imported. Refusing the whole button for one clash put this rule out of a teacher's reach: they had to notice which row it was and untick it. Import is offered while at least one ticked course can come across.
oneCourseFailingDoesNotStopTheRest.nothingHalfMade: Whatever was being made when a course failed - or when the teacher stopped it - is UNLOCKED and then removed, in that order. removeItem and rm -rf both refuse a locked tree, and a half-made folder the teacher can delete from neither the app nor Finder is a worse outcome than the failure that produced it. Possible at all only because the lock is the last step of making a reference course.

olderLayout.note: Issue #254. Russell's OLDER way of keeping a course (2023-24): one Obsidian folder per class SECTION - ICS3U-S1-2023-24 - holding its Thread N folders of class pages at the top, Home.md and All Prior Classes.md beside them, and the shared folders and pages (Tasks, Concepts, Media, Learning Goals.md...) reached through LINKS into a sibling folder whose name ends in 'Shared'. No course_config.json anywhere. The same File > Import Courses for Reference... sheet recognises it (Russell, decision 4: one door), and each class folder becomes ONE single-section reference course (decision 1) made by exactly the code every other import ends in - so the marker, the neutralisation, the fifteen refusals and the lock all apply unchanged. Asked ONLY when the chosen folder is not the modern shape: a folder holding a courses folder or a course's settings is always read the modern way, whatever else is in it.
olderLayout.treeEntries: A plain string is a file (content 'something'); one ending '/' is an empty folder; {"file": path, "changed": "YYYY-MM-DD"} is a file last changed that day; {"file": path, "text": "..."} is a file with that content; {"link": path, "to": null} is a link whose target does not exist, and {"link": path, "to": "<path in the tree>"} one that resolves. Links are NAMES to every rule here and are never followed, which is why the dangling and the resolving forms must produce identical outcomes.

recognition.rule: A PAGE FOLDER is a real folder named 'Thread <digits>' (any case, one space) holding at least one .md file DIRECTLY inside it. An OLDER CLASS FOLDER is a real folder that (a) has a real .obsidian folder, (b) has at least one page folder, (c) holds no course_config.json, and (d) whose name does not end in ' Shared'. Accepted: a class folder itself (offered alone, ticked); a folder whose children include at least one class folder (the 'Class Website' folder); and a folder with a child named exactly 'Class Website' that is such a folder (the course folder above it). The shared folder chosen by mistake - a folder named '... Shared' beside class folders - is refused with its own sentence. Anything else is refused noCoursesThere, exactly as before. Every entry is asked about WITHOUT following a link: a child that is a link is never a class folder and never a shared folder.
recognition.why: (a) AND (b), because each alone admits a real folder that is not a class. Measured on the real folders: the course folders above (ICS3U/, ICS4U/, ICD2O/) have Thread N folders of the teacher's PLANNING - subfolders, 0 pages directly inside any of them - and no .obsidian; ICD2O-LCS-LDPS-Collaboration has .obsidian and no Thread folder. All six real class folders pass, with 12 to 17 pages directly in each Thread folder.
recognition.tickedWhenOpened: A class folder chosen on its own: that one. A folder of them: only those NAMED like a class (CODE-YYYY-YY or CODE-Sn-YYYY-YY, the year's two halves consecutive), and of several sections of one course in one school year only the LOWEST section. The others are offered unticked. Ticking S1 and S2 of 2023-24 together opened the sheet with S2 already in trouble under 'You already have a ICS3U kept for reference from 2023-24' - false, since nothing was kept yet, and advice ('Choose a different school year') that is wrong for a second section. S2 is a second import (Russell, decision 1), and the sheet says so beside it with wording.olderLayoutAnotherSectionOfTheSameCourse.

codeAndYear.rule: From the class folder's NAME. The code is the leading five characters when they are three letters, a digit and a letter or digit, followed by the end or by something that is neither, upper-cased. The year is '-YYYY-YY' where YY is the year after YYYY; it becomes the proposed school year when it is one the sheet offers, and otherwise the pages' own dates propose one (referenceCourses.importing.schoolYearProposed). The section is '-S<digits>' followed by '-' or the end. looksLikeAClass is the name being EXACTLY CODE-YYYY-YY or CODE-Sn-YYYY-YY. The year stays editable in the sheet; the code does not, and the section number is NOT carried - every import is section1.

sharedFolder.rule: Found by NAME, never by following a link (Russell, decision 2): among the class folder's SIBLINGS, the real folders - never a link - whose name ends in ' Shared' and begins with the class's code and a dash. One candidate is it, whatever year its name carries. Several: the one whose '-YYYY-YY' is the class's, and otherwise none. The class's top-level LINK NAMES are the manifest of what it showed: a name is found when the shared folder holds a real entry of exactly that name (compared composed, as bytes), and ONLY the named entries come across, files and folders alike. The sheet says, before Import, where the shared pages come from or that none were found, and offers 'Choose Shared Folder...' on every such row - ALSO when one was found by its name (Russell, decision 7: a wrong match must be correctable). Nothing found and nothing chosen imports anyway and says what is missing.
sharedFolder.why: Measured: in every real case the class's link names equal the shared folder's top-level entries exactly (0 missing, 0 extra, 0 colliding with a real entry), so the name match is exact on the real data. Following the links was REJECTED: all 18 of ICS3U's point at a folder that no longer exists.
sharedFolder.chosenByHand: A folder the teacher chooses is REFUSED, and the row keeps what it had, when it is the folder this window has open (or inside it, or holding it - the three existing sentences), when it is itself a class folder, or when it holds none of the class's names. Measured why 'holds at least one name' is not enough on its own: ICS4U-2023-24, itself a class, holds 14 of ICS3U S1's 18 names, and ICD2O-2023-24 Shared holds 15. A chosen folder whose name carries a DIFFERENT course code is accepted with a warning beside the row (wording.olderLayoutChosenFolderIsForAnotherCourse): Russell kept things where he kept them, and a refusal would leave him no way through.

placement.rule: Where everything lands in the new course, source path -> destination. Thread N folders go under section1/ with their names unchanged and are the per_section_folders. Home.md becomes section1/index.md - the ONE rename, bytes unchanged (Russell, decision 6); with no Home.md a root index.md takes its place, and with both, index.md is left out. All Prior Classes.md goes to section1/ as the one per_section_files entry. .obsidian comes to the course root WITHOUT plugins/ and WITHOUT community-plugins.json. Every other real top-level entry of the class folder, and every shared entry the class's links named, goes to the course root under its own name. Every LINK, at any depth and in either folder, is left out. A top-level link of the class is a NAME and is either replaced by the shared folder's real entry or counted as missing; everything else left out - a link below the top, a link inside a shared entry, anything whose name the course uses for itself (section1, course_config.json, and a shared index.md) - is a LOSS, and is COUNTED and NAMED in the sheet's summary (wording.olderLayoutLeftOut) and on the trail, and the import is not reported as complete (expectLost). The add-ons are said once, for every older class, instead. When nothing supplies Media an empty Media folder is made. Every page is byte-identical, dg-* keys and all (Russell, decision 3).
placement.whyThreadFoldersSitAtSection1: Home.md embeds ![[Thread 4/Day 15]] - a PATH link, which Quartz resolves from the content root. The build copies each per_section_folders entry to content/<name>, so section1/Thread 4/ becomes content/Thread 4/ and the link resolves as it did in the class folder. Measured, simulating Quartz v4.5.0's shortest resolution over the planned content root: ICS3U S1 + shared, 1,586 of 1,587 links and embeds resolve (the one is an absolute path to a folder that no longer exists); without the shared folder, 57 of 186. Nesting them under section1/All Classes/ was REJECTED: it breaks every one of those path embeds.
placement.whyTheFrontPageIsRenamed: With no section1/index.md the build writes no index.html and the preview's watcher waits for it forever. 0 links in the real pages name Home, so nothing points at the old name.
placement.whyNoLinkComesAcross: A reference course must hold no link: the lock cannot lock through one, the census does not count one (so a course holding a live link into iCloud reported 'everything that should be locked is'), and the preview cannot follow one out of courses/. MEASURED, before this change: the copier copied a symlink AS a link, dangling or not, and counted it as a file - pointed at an ICD2O class, today's route would have made a reference course whose shared content was live links into iCloud. The planner leaves every link out and the copier REFUSES one on this route as well, so a future planner bug fails loudly.
placement.whyTheAddOnsStayBehind: MEASURED (key names only, never a value): every real class folder carries .obsidian/plugins/digitalgarden/data.json with a non-empty githubToken, and community-plugins.json enables that add-on. Copied, the credential would land in the working folder, travel into every backup and archive zip of the course, and - once Obsidian trusts the vault's add-ons - give a publish command outside all fifteen of Plantoir's refusals. The rest of .obsidian (appearance, app.json, themes) comes, so the course opens normally and ReferenceReadingView still sets reading view. The shared folder's own .obsidian never comes. Since #255 this is the rule EVERY route keeps (referenceCourses.obsidianAddOns), which also leaves publish.json, and the add-ons are skipped by the walk rather than filtered after it, so an unreadable folder inside one no longer refuses the class.

olderLayout.whatThePreviewShows: Every page except those saying draft: true. The class pages carry Obsidian Digital Garden's keys (dg-publish, dg-home-link, dg-home), which Plantoir does not read, and the shared pages carry NO dg-publish key at all - measured: 78 of 78 ICS3U shared pages, 1 ICS4U page, 1 ICD2O page - and were therefore never published under Digital Garden, which published only dg-publish: true. Three pages say dg-publish: false. So unlike a modern reference course (neutralises.kept), a preview of one of these shows MORE than students saw. Accepted by Russell for v1.3.0 (answer 5); the pages stay byte-identical and what dg-* keys should mean when a page is copied into a live course is a separate issue.
olderLayout.sectionTitle: Every import is section1, so the preview's 'S1' marker would name the wrong section for an S2. There is no config key that says which section a single-section course WAS, and one was not invented: the import writes show_section_marker false for section1 (an existing, documented key), so the preview is titled with the code alone, and course_name carries the class folder's name (ICS3U-S2-2023-24). Two sections of one course cannot both be kept under one school year - the shelf rule - so S2 is filed under Other or another year, or not kept.

quartzCheckoutLayout.note: Issue #256. Russell's 2024-25 way of keeping a course: one whole WEBSITE folder per class section - ~/Documents/Class Websites/2024-25/ICS3U/S1 - holding the program that built the site (quartz/: quartz.config.ts, package.json, the program, public/, .quartz-cache, scripts) and the pages under quartz/content/source-<code>/{shared, s1, s2}. The folder Obsidian opened, quartz/content, is mostly LINKS into source-<code>, plus vault-<code>-s<N> folders made of links for editing. The iCloud folder he named in the issue (2024-25/Old ICS3U/Class Websites) holds only two Finder shortcuts, S1 and S2, leading to those website folders. The same File > Import Courses for Reference... sheet recognises it, THIRD - after the modern shapes and #254's olderLayout - and ONLY THE FIRST SECTION of a course kept this way comes across (Russell, 2026-09-23), as one single-section reference course made by exactly the code every other import ends in.
quartzCheckoutLayout.treeEntries: As olderLayout.treeEntries, plus: {"link": path, "text": "<link text>"} is a link whose text is exactly that (relative, as the real ones are: ./source-ics3u/s1/index.md); {"alias": path, "to": "<path in the tree>"} is a Finder shortcut (an alias file made with bookmarkData(options: .suitableForBookmarkFile) + writeBookmarkData) to that entry, {"alias": path, "to": null} one whose target was a folder that was then deleted, and "thenLock": "<path in the tree>" makes that folder unreadable (mode 000) after the shortcut is made - the shape of a refused Documents permission. recognition.rule: A WEBSITE FOLDER is a real folder holding a real folder quartz/, which holds a regular file quartz.config.ts and a real folder content/. Its COURSE PAGES FOLDER is the ONE real folder directly in content/ named source-<code> (any case), <code> five characters of the Ontario shape (olderLayout.codeAndYear's rule), holding at least one real s<digits> folder. A website folder with no course pages folder is not a course and is left out of every list (Math Club - Russell, 2026-09-23); with two, its row says checkoutLayoutMoreThanOneCourse. A SHORTCUT is an entry that Finder marks as an alias (isAliasFileKey) AND that lstat calls a regular file: a symbolic link also answers isAliasFileKey true, and resolving one follows it, so a link is NEVER a shortcut. Resolved with [.withoutUI, .withoutMounting]; when that fails, the bookmark's STORED path and kind are read without resolving and the stored path asked about with lstat: a stored FILE is 'leadsToAFile', EACCES/EPERM 'couldNotBeOpened', a path under /Volumes whose disk is not mounted 'diskNotConnected', anything else 'gone'. Tried in this order: (1) a shortcut chosen on its own - to a website folder: that one; one that leads nowhere or to a file: refused with its sentence; (2) a website folder, or its quartz/ or quartz/content/ folder: that one; (3) anything else inside a website folder's quartz/, found by walking the chosen path's ancestors: a later section's pages (content/source-<code>/s<M> or content/vault-<code>-s<M>, M not 1) refused checkoutLayoutOnlyTheFirstSection, anything else refused checkoutLayoutChooseTheWholeFolder - never resolved upward; (4) the CANDIDATES in the chosen folder (website folders, shortcuts leading to one, and shortcuts to a FOLDER that cannot be read through - a shortcut to a file is passed over as a file is) and in each of its children: readable candidates directly inside AND in a child, or in two or more children, refused checkoutLayoutChooseOneCourseAtATime; directly inside only, that folder; in exactly one child only, that child; only unreadable shortcuts, that folder (or the one child holding them), each shown with its reason. Looking at a child's candidates means listing the child's entries: a real folder among them is asked whether it is a website folder (lstat of its quartz/quartz.config.ts and quartz/content, and of content/source-*/s<N>), and a shortcut among them is RESOLVED (without a dialog and without mounting). (5) Only when all of that found nothing: the chosen folder's grandchildren - a folder two levels down holding a SHORTCUT that leads to a website folder (the school year's folder in iCloud, LCS/2024-25, whose Old ICS3U/Class Websites holds S1 and S2) - refused checkoutLayoutChooseACourseFolderInside, never imported from; the first such shortcut ends the look. At that depth only shortcuts are asked about, never the folders beside them, so a broad folder chosen by mistake does not become a look inside every folder three levels down. Nothing: nil, and noCoursesThere exactly as before. Every entry is asked about WITHOUT following a link, and nothing deeper than that is looked at.
recognition.why: Measured on Russell's folders: every shape of them - the shortcut folder, Old ICS3U, 2024-25, ICS3U, S1, S1/quartz, quartz/content, source-ics3u, vault-ics3u-s2, Math Club - returned nothing from the first two routes, so this route can never take a folder either of them reads. The children are counted rather than any folder NAME trusted: 2024-25 holds ICS3U/ and ICS4U/ (several courses) while Old ICS3U holds exactly one child of shortcuts (Class Websites) beside planning folders and a shortcut to a PDF.
recognition.section: The section a website folder built is, first, the one its front page's link TEXT names - content/index.md -> [./]source-<code>/s<N>/index.md with s<N> present (read with destinationOfSymbolicLink, never followed; S2's own publish script rewrote exactly these links to make S2's site); then the folder's own name S<N> when s<N> is present; then the only s<N> there is; otherwise the row says checkoutLayoutWhichSection. Measured: the front page and the name agree in 5 of 5 real website folders. Only section 1 comes across: a later section chosen on its own is REFUSED checkoutLayoutOnlyTheFirstSection, and in a folder of them it is SHOWN with that sentence, unticked.
