placement.rule: Read ONLY from the website folder pointed at (or the one its shortcut leads to): its own source-<code>/s1 and source-<code>/shared, BY NAME, walked with lstat and never followed. s1/* goes to section1/ unchanged (index.md is already the front page, so nothing is renamed; All Classes lands at section1/All Classes, the modern layout's own place); shared/* goes to the course root, Media included; content/.obsidian comes WITHOUT plugins/, community-plugins.json and publish.json (referenceCourses.obsidianAddOns, the rule every route keeps; skipped, never walked). A real entry at the top of content/ other than .obsidian, source-* and vault-* (0 measured) comes to the root as shared. The links at the top of content/ are a MANIFEST: each link's TEXT, worked out against content/ as a path, must be source-<code>/shared/<its own name> or source-<code>/s1/<its own name>, and that entry must be there - then it is 'replaced by what it showed', machinery; otherwise it is a LOSS. Also a loss, and named: a link anywhere inside the pages or inside .obsidian (outside plugins/), a shared entry with the same name as one of the section's own (nameTheSectionUses - the build would put both at content/<name>), a shared entry named index.md, section1 or course_config.json (nameTheCourseUses), and no s1/index.md (noFrontPage). Settings: course_code, course_name '<CODE> S1', one section, shared_folders (top folders except Media and dot-folders), shared_files (top regular files except dot-files), per_section_folders and per_section_files (s1's top folders, and its files except index.md), expandable, hidden [Media], include_curriculum_coverage false, show_section_marker section1 false - #254's - and unit_word when unitWord finds one. placement.whyTheCopyInThisFolder: S1's and S2's copies of source-ics3u DIFFER (335 entries, measured by SHA-1). S2's publish script (synclink) rsyncs S1's content into S2 before each S2 publish and re-points the section links, so each copy is exactly what that website folder's site was last built from; S1's is where both sections were edited and carries 2025-26 changes. placement.whyNoLinkComesAcross: As olderLayout.placement.whyNoLinkComesAcross, and here the links would even resolve: that is exactly why the copier still never copies one. The pages are selected by name; a link is a manifest entry and nothing more.
placement.whyUnitWord: The build's post-pass (_sync_non_class_pages_created) restamps the created date of every page it does not recognise as a class page by class_page_pattern(unit_word). With the key absent the word is Unit, no page of these is a class page, and every lesson in the preview gets the same date. So the import writes unit_word when the class folder's pages agree on one word.

leftBehind.rule: Machinery, counted by kind and named on the trail, NEVER a loss: it never makes an import 'imported with something missing' and never appears in the summary's list. A Windows implementation must keep leftBehind and lost as two lists (#254's first cut lumped them).

wording.checkoutLayoutRule: The checkoutLayout* sentences are said only about a class kept in the 2024-25 layout, a whole website folder per class (quartzCheckoutLayout above). {place} is where the pages are read from: ~/... inside the home folder, the whole path otherwise. {shortcut} is a Finder shortcut's own name - 'shortcut' is the one word allowed about how the folders were joined, because the teacher made them in Finder; none says alias, link, vault, checkout or Quartz. checkoutLayoutOnlyTheFirstSection is both a row's reason and the refusal when a later section is chosen on its own, {section} its number. A row reached through a shortcut says checkoutLayoutReadThroughShortcut, any other checkoutLayoutReadFrom. checkoutLayoutOnlyPagesComeAcross is said once under the list and in the summary whenever such a row is there. A loss reuses olderLayoutLeftOut; a link that showed something else is one of its {names} as checkoutLayoutWhatALinkShowed, {name} the link's own name and {place} its own text with './' taken off and a home-folder path written from '~' (never the account name). checkoutLayoutChooseACourseFolderInside is the refusal for a school year's folder whose courses' shortcuts are two levels down (recognition.rule step 5).
wording.olderLayoutRule: The olderLayout* sentences are said only about a class kept in the older folder-per-class layout (olderLayout above). {names} is the missing names in a stable order joined as 'A, B and C' (in olderLayoutLeftOut, the paths left out, and with {count} 1 the sentence reads '1 of its files or folders was not brought across'); {count} is how many shared folders and pages the class used (in olderLayoutLeftOut, how many were left out); alsoTickedForThatYear is said beside a ticked row whose code and year clash ONLY with a row ticked above it in the same sheet - nothing is kept yet, so codeAlreadyInThatYear ('You already have...') would be false - unless both are older-layout classes named as sections of the course, which get olderLayoutAnotherSectionOfTheSameCourse; {folder} is the row above, {course} the code; olderLayoutLeftOut is added to a summary line after olderLayoutImportedWithSharedMissing, or after 'imported' and a full stop; {code} is the code a chosen folder's name carries. None of them says how the shared folder was reached from the class - a teacher kept folders, and folders are what they are told about - and none says vault, link or add-on settings' contents.
wording.rule: {course} is the code a TEACHER reads - ICS4U, never the folder name; {folder} is the folder they chose, by its own name, because 'that folder' means nothing once the chooser has closed. The calm note about the pages being locked (referenceCourses.wording.pagesAreLocked) is shown in this sheet too, where the teacher is deciding rather than after the fact.
wording.machineryCheck: No sentence here names a symlink, a build output, a script, a container or a flag. Nothing says 'cannot' where 'is not' will do. The size a teacher reads is the size that will be COPIED, with last year's built website already taken out of it.

copyingAPageBetweenCourses.note: Copying ONE page out of one course and into another, with the pictures and files it shows - 'Copy a Page from This Course...' on any course row in the sidebar. Shared because both apps offer it, both write the same frontmatter, and the one thing it must never get wrong is the same on both: a copy that turns up where students can read it. Issue #207.
copyingAPageBetweenCourses.rule: A copy ALWAYS arrives hidden from students, in every section of the course it lands in. Nothing already in the destination is ever changed, renamed or written over. Anything the page names that is not carried is LISTED - never dropped in silence.

whereItIsOffered.why: The source is only ever READ, so a course kept for reference offers this for the same reason it offers Preview and Back Up Now. It is the point of keeping the course rather than an exception to its being frozen. The DESTINATION is never a reference course and never the source itself.
whereItIsOffered.theDestinationList: The courses the teacher teaches, by the code a teacher reads, minus the source course. A course kept for reference is never a destination: it is frozen.

whatMayBeCopied.rule: A page directly inside a TOP-LEVEL shared folder of the source course, and nothing else.
whatMayBeCopied.nested: Only the folder's own top level is listed. Measured: 0 of 452 real shared pages, 0 of 38 example-content payloads and 0 of 2,038 skeleton pages sit in a subfolder, and build_site.py's discover_shared_items scans the course root only. So a source subfolder path is never mirrored and no folder is ever created for one.
whatMayBeCopied.theFolderItLandsIn: A TOP-LEVEL shared folder of the DESTINATION that is both listed in shared_folders AND present on disk. A listed folder that is not on disk is not offered, because writing into it would mean creating it. The question starts on the source page's own folder when the destination has one of that name, and on the first otherwise.

whatIsNeverCopied.why: A class belongs to a timetable. Landing one in another course would need a date, a number and a whole second set of refusals. Russell, explicitly: class pages are omitted by design.
An index is the way IN to a folder, not a page anybody links to.

whatIsNeverCopied.what: a page at the course root
whatIsNeverCopied.why: Russell's rule. Those are the course's own front matter - Learning Goals, Key Links - and they are not folder content.

whatIsNeverCopied.what: a page inside a section<N> folder
whatIsNeverCopied.why: It belongs to one section's classes rather than to the course.

whatIsNeverCopied.what: anything in Media that nothing on the page points at
whatIsNeverCopied.why: The page's pictures and files come along; the rest of the course's Media does not.

hidden.rule: The copied page carries publishForSection<N>: false for EVERY section the destination has, and then a plain publish: false as the LAST line of its frontmatter.
hidden.theOrderIsLoadBearing: Per-section keys FIRST, then the plain key. Measured: writing publish: false first makes the per-section writer a complete no-op - its 'already says it' gate reads the plain key and returns the text unchanged, so NO publishForSection key is written at all.
hidden.whyThePlainKeyAtAll: It is what keeps the copy hidden in a section the destination gains LATER, by any route. Measured: all 156 of one real course's shared pages, composed with the per-section keys alone, come out VISIBLE in a section 4 they were never told about, because Quartz publishes a page that says nothing.
hidden.whatComesOffFirst: The source's own publishForSection<N>, draftSection<N> and createdSection<N>, and the plain publish: and draft:. The plain pair is stripped with the READER's key matcher and its continuation rule, never a prefix test: a naive strip of a draft: whose value sits on the line BELOW it orphans that line, YAML folds it into the last key written as the plain scalar 'false true', and the build does not hide a string that is not 'false' - so the page is PUBLISHED. Measured. The house format drops the plain keys anyway: setup_course.py's per_section_frontmatter removes plain created/publish/draft when it splits a page into per-section pairs.
hidden.theOldSectionTwoKeys: draftSectionTwo and createdForSectionTwo - the 2024-25 website-folder layout's keys for a class's second section, and the only per-section keys a census of all four of that layout's real copies found (800 and 655 lines over 1,338 pages) - come off with the plain pair, with the same matcher and continuation rule. Russell's decision, 2026-09-23 (#256). No build since reads them, and a page still carrying draftSectionTwo would be refused by the builder-agreement guard, whose language was left unchanged: they are stripped before it is asked.
hidden.whatIsKept: Everything else the teacher wrote, created: included. A page copied from last year shows last year's date until they change it; they see the page in Obsidian before publishing, and silently rewriting a date in their own frontmatter is the larger sin.
hidden.sectionsAreReReadBeforeWriting: The destination's section numbers are read from course_config.json again immediately before the text is composed, rather than taken from the plan. A section added in another window between the two would otherwise leave the copy with nothing said about it.

readBackAndDelete.rule: After the page is written it is READ BACK FROM DISK and asked, for every section the destination has AND for one section number it does not have, whether it is hidden. The test is 'is not hidden', not 'is visible', so a value the app cannot read counts as failure. If the answer is not certainly hidden everywhere, the file just written is DELETED and the page is reported as not copied.
readBackAndDelete.nothingTouchesThePageAfterIt: Media names are settled and the embeds rewritten BEFORE the page is written, so the read-back is the last thing that touches the page's bytes. The locked flag is cleared BEFORE the read-back, because a locked file could not be deleted - and deleting it is what the guard has to be able to do.
readBackAndDelete.why: This is the last line of defence on the one failure that reports success: a page that arrives visible and is deployed to students. It errs toward no page at all.
readBackAndDelete.theChecklistIsInTheFUTURE: The screen that lists the linked pages is the one whose purpose is to let a teacher change their mind, so EVERY sentence on it is in the future - the header, the size line, the rename line and every SKIP - and each has a twin keyed separately from the result screen's. Measured on the real app: it said 'Copied 11 pages...' (the result sentence) above a Copy button, and it said of a page nothing had been done to yet: 'is already in this course, so it was left as it is'.
readBackAndDelete.theChecklistsROWSdoNotMOVE: The rows are the full candidate set the FIRST plan found, in a stable order; only the numbers and the sentences below them are recomputed from the ticks. Drawing the list from the latest plan made an unticked page VANISH - a teacher could not put it back, or even see what they had turned off. Seen on the real app: unticking 'Command-Line Projects' removed its row. Tick state A to B and back to A must give the identical plan.
readBackAndDelete.aPageSHOWNinsideanotherCOMESALONGwhileTh: A page embedded with ![[...]] is ticked and cannot be unticked WHILE any page that shows it is coming along, and becomes an ordinary row when none is. Leaving it behind would put a hole in the page that shows it; keeping it locked after that page is gone would be a row the teacher cannot explain.
readBackAndDelete.theCHOSENpageIsTheFIRSTROW: Ticked, not untickable, and labelled as the page they chose - so the header's count and the list agree. It said '3 pages' over two rows.
readBackAndDelete.whatTheReadBackCannotSeeOnItsOwn: The app's reader is not the one that decides what students see, and two shapes were REPRODUCED where the two split - the copy certified hidden by the app and PUBLISHED by the builder. (1) A settings block closed by an INDENTED ---: the app trims leading spaces before testing a fence, python-frontmatter's boundary does not, so it finds no end, reads nothing, and Quartz publishes a page that says nothing (the divergence is issue #188). (2) A block carrying a YAML ANCHOR or ALIAS: taking the plain publish: line out can orphan an alias the rest of the block refers to, frontmatter.load then raises, build_site.py prints a warning and RETURNS, and the page reaches Quartz unresolved. Measured incidence across 777 real pages: ZERO of either. So the read-back ALSO asks a second question. It is stated as ONE INVARIANT plus a small REGULAR LANGUAGE - anchored line patterns over an explicit CHARACTER whitelist - because a whitelist of line SHAPES still admits arbitrary characters, and an extended fuzz found 3,311 of 60,000 pages certified and not hidden on exactly that: a YAML-1.1 bool word as a key, U+2028/U+2029/U+0085 in a value, a C0 control, a quote inside a double-quoted scalar, a plain scalar opening with a flow indicator, and a list item at column 0. KEY: [A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]* and never a bool or null word. LINE: blank, # comment, 'key:', 'key: VALUE', or an indented '- VALUE' under a 'key:' line. VALUE: a plain scalar opening with a letter, digit or underscore and containing no ': ', no ' #' and no trailing ':'; or a double-quoted scalar with no quote and no backslash; or a single-quoted scalar with no quote; or []. ANYWHERE: no C0 control but the line break, no DEL, no U+0085/U+2028/U+2029, no U+FEFF after the first scalar, no U+FFFD. It is far narrower than YAML, deliberately; a refused page is said so in a plain sentence and can always be copied by hand. The language was derived from a census of all 12,668 shipped and real pages (17 distinct keys, no control characters, no value containing ': ') so the false-refusal count stays at zero. THE INVARIANT itself: EVERY key that hides the copy must lie inside the region the BUILD reads as frontmatter, that region must carry no OTHER visibility key, the two readers must agree about where it ENDS, and every top-level line in it must be a shape the build's YAML parser reads. Anything else is not copied, with wording.thePageIsWrittenInAWayPlantoirCannotBeSureOf. Three failures were reproduced end to end and the invariant catches all three: an indented closing fence (#188); a BLOCK SCALAR carrying a horizontal rule (description: | ... ---), where the app closes INSIDE the scalar and inserts its publish: false there while the build reads the whole block and takes the source's publish: true from the bottom - the copy reached students in section 1 while the summary said it was hidden; and a block only one of them closes, so the file becomes several documents and the parser gives up. A benign block scalar is NOT refused. MEASURED against the real python-frontmatter 1.3.0 / PyYAML 6.0.3 + publish.ts rule: three seeds of an extended grammar generator at 60,000 pages each, three seeds of a further extension, two seeds of the original grammar, a 16,192-shape cross product, the 11,891 shipped pages, the 777 real pages and the 172 ICS4U shared pages - certified-and-not-hidden is 0 on every one, and false refusals are 0 of 11,891 shipped and 0 of 777 real. An & or a * inside a VALUE is not an anchor - four shipped pages were refused for a title containing '&' before that was made precise. A refusal here is always right.
readBackAndDelete.theDeleteIsChecked: A page that fails the read-back is removed, and the REMOVAL is checked. '... was not copied' is the strongest promise this feature makes, and making it on an unchecked delete would let a page nobody could prove hidden sit in the teacher's course while they were told it was not there - an immutable parent folder is the realistic way it fails. When the removal fails the teacher is told something DIFFERENT, the file's path is named, and the trail line says how many could not be removed and must not be deployed.

neverOverwritten.everyWriteIsCreateExclusive: A page is created with O_CREAT | O_EXCL and a picture with copyfile's COPYFILE_CLONE, which implies COPYFILE_EXCL. Measured on an APFS case-insensitive volume: both refuse a destination that already exists, one differing only by CASE, one differing only by extension case, and one differing only by how an accent is spelled. There is no check-then-write window.
neverOverwritten.aLateCollisionIsASkip: A file that appears between the plan and the write is reported as the ordinary 'already here' skip, in the same words the index would have produced - never as an error and never as an overwrite.
neverOverwritten.theNameIndex: A page name already ANYWHERE in the destination course - any folder, shared or per-section, at any depth - means the page is not copied and is named in the summary; the links then lead to the page that is already there. Never renamed, never overwritten. Names are compared with the .md dropped, NFC-composed and case-folded. Composed as well as folded because AssistSectionGraph.normalized only lowercases, and on a case-SENSITIVE volume the file system would not refuse the write while Quartz would still slug the two pages to one page.
neverOverwritten.theBuiltWebsiteIsNotIndexed: .merged_output, node_modules, .git, .quartz-cache, .cache and .obsidian are left out of the index: everything in them is generated.

namesAreBytes.rule: A file name is carried as the BYTES the file system gave and written back as those same bytes. It is turned into text only to show somebody, and normalised only to COMPARE.
namesAreBytes.why: Measured on macOS 26.6: reading a name back through readdir, FileManager.contentsOfDirectory(at:) and contentsOfDirectory(atPath:) all preserve the bytes, but WRITING through a URL built with appendingPathComponent DECOMPOSES it - a name stored as c3 a9 was written out as 65 cc 81. The page that embeds the picture still spells the name the old way, so on a volume that compares names byte for byte the embed stops resolving and the picture vanishes from the built site with no error anywhere. Four files in one real course are of that shape.
namesAreBytes.renamedFilesToo: A file brought in under a new name keeps the SOURCE's byte form for the part of the name that came from the source; only an ASCII suffix is added, before the last dot.

picturesAndFiles.whereTheyAreFound: Every place the page names something local: ![[x.png]] embeds, [[x.pdf]] links that point at a FILE rather than a page, HTML src and href attributes, and Markdown link destinations. Measured across 777 real markdown files: 1,474 embeds (1,274 of them media), 1,222 links of which 250 point at a file (235 PDFs), 5 HTML attributes naming a local file - one of them a live 1.1 MB picture on a copyable page - and 526 Markdown links, every one of them https://.
picturesAndFiles.fencedCodeIsLeftAlone: A name inside a fenced code block is prose about a file rather than a use of one, and rewriting it would edit an example a teacher wrote. Inline code spans are not tracked, which is the same known gap WikiLinkRewriter has.
picturesAndFiles.sameNameSameFile: Reused silently. Nothing is copied and nothing is said, beyond the count.
picturesAndFiles.sameNameDifferentFile: The incoming file comes in under a NEW name and only the COPIED page is pointed at it. The teacher's own file is untouched. The new name is '<name> (from <source course folder>)<extension>' - the course's FOLDER name, because every picture comes from Media and saying so would say nothing, while ICS4U-2025 says which course it came out of. If that name is taken, a number is added; and if a bounded search still finds nothing free, THE PAGE IS NOT COPIED and says so. That last part is not tidiness: the destination already HAS a file of that name with different bytes - which is why a new name was needed - so a page written with the original name would show the teacher their own DIFFERENT picture, which is the one direction this feature must never err in. Merely listing the file said the opposite about a link that leads somewhere wrong.
picturesAndFiles.invisibleSpacesAreFoldedOnTheWayINOnly: Resolving a reference against the SOURCE's Media folds U+00A0, U+202F and U+2007 to an ordinary space, so a link typed with real spaces finds a file whose name carries a no-break one. The DESTINATION name index does not fold them, so a destination holding a<NBSP>b.png and an incoming a b.png end up side by side with names that look identical. Nothing is overwritten and nothing is lost, which is the safe direction; measured, and left as it is rather than made cleverer.
picturesAndFiles.comparedBySizeThenBytes: Contents are compared only when the sizes match, and are read in chunks: a real picture here can be hundreds of megabytes.
picturesAndFiles.theRewriteIsVerified: After the embeds are rewritten the page is scanned AGAIN with the same scanner, and if it still names any file that was renamed the PAGE IS NOT COPIED and says so. Direction of error: no page at all, rather than a page showing the teacher's own DIFFERENT picture under the name the copy wanted.
picturesAndFiles.theMediaFolderIsTheOneFolderMade: If the destination has no Media folder it is created. It is not a folder a teacher chooses or can rename - Plantoir looks after it - and the site-health repair already creates it when it is missing. No other folder is ever created.

linksLeadingNowhere.rule: Anything the page names that is neither carried nor already in the destination is LISTED for the teacher, in the words the page used.
linksLeadingNowhere.aFileFoundOnlyByFoldingInvisibleSpaces: Carried under its REAL name AND listed. Measured in a real course: a page links to a PDF with ordinary spaces while the file in Media carries a no-break space after each en-dash, so the link does not resolve in the SOURCE either and the teacher may want to fix it.

theBackup.oncePerSheetNotOncePerPress: Taken before the first write of a sheet session. Measured on a real course with the app's own zip command: 9.7 s and 467 MB, because Media is not excluded from an archive. Five presses of 'Copy another' would be fifty seconds of waiting and 2.3 GB of copies - and a second backup taken after the first copy is a way back that already contains the first copy.
theBackup.offTheMainActor: The zip runs off the caller's actor with a calm stated wait. On the mac that takes @concurrent rather than merely nonisolated async, for the reason referenceCourses.frozen.offTheMainActor records.
theBackup.madeByTheTeacher: It is a teacher's backup, so it is never pruned: only the assistant's own backups are. Its file name is shown at the end and goes on the trail, the way a section restore's does.
theBackup.theSourceIsNeverBackedUp: Nothing is written to the source course - no backup, no lease, no cache.

refusals.how: asked again on the main actor immediately before the first write

refusals.when: the destination's shared folders are all missing from disk, so a page has nowhere to land - and no folder is ever created for this
a copy of the destination course could not be saved - nothing is written
there is no other course to copy into
the source has no pages in shared folders

copyingAPageBetweenCourses.notRefusedWhileAPreviewIsRunning: A preview only READS. The narrow 'is a deploy running' question is asked rather than the broad 'is this course busy' one, which is the same distinction the site-health repair learned the hard way.
copyingAPageBetweenCourses.theCopyArrivesUnlocked: Every page written and every picture copied has the locked flag cleared, even when the source is a course kept for reference whose files all carry it. A page a teacher cannot edit, with no explanation, reads as 'the app is broken'.
copyingAPageBetweenCourses.notOnAnyToolSurface: Russell, explicitly: no MCP tool, no local-assistant tool, no tool-surface change at all. It is deterministic code reached from a menu, and adding a tool is a routing change.

wording.rule: {course} is the code a TEACHER reads - ICS4U, never the folder name. Plain words for the things a teacher can see: pages, pictures and files, folders, courses. Never a word about how it is done. A site is DEPLOYED and a page is PUBLISHED.
wording.machineryCheck: No sentence here may contain: frontmatter, wikilink, embed, media folder, walk, graph, script, container, toolchain, docker, yaml, symlink, actor, thread.
wording.menuItem: Copy a Page from This Course…
wording.noPagesMatch: No page of that name in this course.
wording.copiesStartHidden: Copies start hidden, so nothing changes on any website until you publish them.
wording.datesAreKept: The pages keep the dates they had.
wording.nothingIsWrittenOver: Nothing already in that course is changed or written over.
wording.thereIsNoCourseToCopyInto: There is no other course to copy into yet
wording.alsoCopyLinkedPages: Also copy the pages this page links to
wording.willCopy: This will copy {pages} pages into {course}, in {folder}.
wording.willBringPicturesAndFilesInAll: It will bring {count} pictures and files, {size}.
wording.picturesWillComeInUnderANewName: {count} will have the same name as something different already here, so they will come in under new names.
wording.willBeLeftAsItIs: “{page}” is already in this course, so it will be left as it is — links will lead to the one that is here.
wording.aClassPageWillBeLeftAlone: “{page}” is one of that course's classes, so it will be left where it is.
wording.anIndexPageWillNotBeCopied: “{page}” is the way in to a folder rather than a page, so it will not be copied.
wording.aPageAtTheCourseRootWillNotBeCopied: “{page}” sits outside the course's folders, so it will not be copied.
wording.aPageInsideOneSectionsFolderWillNotBeCop: “{page}” belongs to one section's classes, so it will not be copied.
wording.thePageCouldNotBeRead: “{page}” could not be read, so it will not be copied.
wording.embeddedPagesAlwaysComeAlong: This page is shown inside another one, so it comes along.
wording.aClassPageWasLeftAlone: “{page}” is one of that course's classes, so it was left where it is.
wording.anIndexPageIsNotCopied: “{page}” is the way in to a folder rather than a page, so it was not copied.
wording.aPageAtTheCourseRootIsNotCopied: “{page}” sits outside the course's folders, so it was not copied.
wording.aPageInsideOneSectionsFolderIsNotCopied: “{page}” belongs to one section's classes, so it was not copied.
wording.theBackupTaken: A copy of {course} from before this is saved as {named}.
wording.picturesAlreadyThere: {count} are already in this course and will be used as they are.
wording.picturesBroughtInUnderANewName: {count} have the same name as something different already here, so they come in under a new name.
wording.aPageOfThatNameIsAlreadyHere: “{page}” is already in this course, so it was left as it is — links will lead to the one that is here.
wording.theseLinksWillNotLeadAnywhereYet: These links will not lead anywhere yet: “{name}”, “{name}”.
wording.thisCourseHasNoPagesToCopy: {course} has no pages in shared folders to copy
wording.thatCourseHasNowhereToPutIt: {course} has no folder for a page to go in yet
wording.theCopyOfTheCourseCouldNotBeSaved: A copy of {course} could not be saved, so nothing was copied. Check there is room on the disk and try again.
wording.thePageIsWrittenInAWayPlantoirCannotBeSu: “{page}” was not copied: its settings are written in a way Plantoir cannot be sure of, and a copy must never turn up where students can read it.
wording.theCopyIsStillThereAndMustBeRemoved: “{page}” could not be shown to be hidden from students and could not be removed again. It is at {path} — take it out before you deploy that course.
wording.theCopyCouldNotBeMadeHidden: “{page}” was not copied: Plantoir could not be certain it would arrive hidden from students, and a copy must never turn up where students can read it.
wording.thePicturesCouldNotBePointedAtTheirNewNa: “{page}” was not copied: one of its pictures had to come in under a new name and Plantoir could not be certain the page would find it.
wording.aPictureCouldNotBeCopied: “{name}” could not be copied, so the page that shows it will not find it.

theTrail.carries: the course the pages came FROM by its folder name, the course and folder they landed in, how many pages and pictures were created, reused, brought in under a new name and left alone, and the backup's file name
theTrail.never: a page's title, a page's contents, a picture's name
theTrail.oneLineAtTheEnd: Written once at the end of a copy, in every outcome. A copy that stopped part way says so in the same line, because the counts already show it. The three refusals record nothing: they answer before anything is touched.

rejected.what: copying several pages at once
rejected.why: Russell, explicitly: not in this release. 'Copy another' covers the second page at the cost of one press.

rejected.what: an MCP tool or a local-assistant tool
rejected.why: Russell, explicitly. Adding a tool is a routing change, and more choices is the classic way a router degrades.

rejected.what: creating a folder in the destination
rejected.why: A new top-level folder would also have to be registered in shared_folders or the site never builds it - a settings decision with its own refusals. Media is the one exception, because Plantoir looks after it.

rejected.what: mirroring a source SUBfolder path
rejected.why: Measured zero: 0 of 452 real shared pages, 0 of 38 payloads and 0 of 2,038 skeleton pages sit in a subfolder. The case never fires, landing flat is one line instead of ten, and it creates nothing.

rejected.what: undo of any kind
rejected.why: The backup is the way back and it is one file. The assistant's change history holds TEXT, so a picture cannot travel through it at all - an undo that took the pages and left 300 MB of images behind would be worse than none.

rejected.what: a backup that leaves Media out, to make it quick
rejected.why: Restoring one would DELETE every picture in the course. The ten seconds buys a way back that is actually a way back.

rejected.what: a progress bar or a size refusal
rejected.why: Measured 879 MB/s on an internal SSD; the worst real copy is 306 files and 302 MB in 0.47 s. The backup is the pause, not the copy. The size is STATED instead, because a refusal would invent a threshold nobody measured.

rejected.what: rewriting links in the copied page to point at pages that were skipped
rejected.why: They already point at the right NAME, and the destination's own page of that name answers them.

builderAgreement.note: Whether the WEBSITE BUILDER would read the composed page's settings block the same way the app does. A composed text that fails this is NOT COPIED, whatever the app's own reader says - the two shapes below were reproduced end to end with the copy certified hidden here and PUBLISHED there. Since #246 (2026-09-25) the builder HIDES a page whose settings it cannot read and names it in a folder-problem finding, where before it published such a page or stopped the whole build - so the cases below that say "reads no keys" or "PUBLISHED" describe what happened BEFORE #246 (unreadablePageSettings has what happens now). The copy is STILL refused: a copy that arrives hidden by accident, and named as a problem on every build, is not a clean copy. Whether this guard can now be relaxed is a follow-up, not part of #246.

cases.why: A teacher's typo. 2025-09-93 resolves as a timestamp and raises a ValueError on construction, so the build reads no keys. Resolving and constructing are two steps and only the second can fail.

cases.why: On a real page of Russell's. It is certified here because its offset carries no colon, so PyYAML does NOT resolve it as a timestamp at all and reads it as a string - which is why the rule follows PyYAML's own patterns rather than refusing everything date-shaped.

savingSettings.rule: A Save writes only the settings THIS window changed since it last read or wrote the course's settings file. Every other setting keeps the value the file has now. Compared per TOP-LEVEL key of course_config.json, never inside a list. After a Save, every other window's copy of that course that has nothing unsaved reads the file again; a copy with unsaved changes is left alone, and its own Save follows the same rule.
savingSettings.why: Issue #265, confirmed by Russell 2026-09-24: two windows were open on one working folder, each holding its own copy of a course's settings, and the Save was a blind whole-file write. Window A saved three sidebar hides; window B, which had not seen that, saved an unrelated setting and the file went back to B's ten hides while both windows said nothing was unsaved - measured with the real CourseConfiguration.swift and a copy of his course. The same stale write came from Add Section, archive, restore, course rename and school year, so the rule is in the ONE write they all use. Per key rather than per list element because merging inside a list needs rules for order and for an item removed on one side and added on the other, and nothing reported needs them. When both sides changed the same key, the Save being made wins and the trail says it replaced a change made elsewhere. Rejected: refusing the Save and reloading (loses what the teacher just did, for a case the trail can record); a file watcher per window (a new moving part for a case the reload-after-Save covers).

workLeases.note: A work lease is a file under courses/.internal/activity/ saying which process is doing what to a course or a folder, so another window, another copy of Plantoir or an assistant working from outside can leave that work alone. Its FORMAT is file-formats.json -> workLease. This block is the rules every READER shares. #245 (the import's staging folders) wrote the first of them - who counts as alive (liveness) - and #156 (builds, previews and deploys, both ways) added the second beside it - who stands in whose way (declining) - rather than a second reader.

liveness.rule: A lease's owner is ALIVE unless one of these says it is gone, asked in this order: the process id is 0 or less; the signal check (kill(pid, 0) on the mac) says there is no such process; the process table says there is no such process; the process has finished and is waiting to be collected (a zombie); the lease records a name and the running process's name is a different one (compared without regard to case, on the first sixteen characters, which is all the mac's table keeps); the lease records a start time and the running process started at a different one. An IMPORT lease with no name line is judged as if it said Plantoir, the only program that ever wrote one (a one-line import lease left by a pre-#245 crash would otherwise be judged on its id alone, and after a restart that id can belong to an unrelated process for the whole uptime - which since #245 refuses every import of the course). A BUILD, PREVIEW or PUBLISH lease with no name line (or an empty one) is not judged here at all: it is treated as GONE before this rule is asked (#156; workLeases.declining), because neither app writes one and Windows' reader calls fewer than two lines stale. A signal answer of 'not permitted' means the process EXISTS and belongs to someone else. A table that cannot be asked means cannot tell, and cannot tell is ALIVE.
liveness.why: The two directions are not equal. Reading a live owner as gone removes somebody's half-made work; reading a gone owner as alive leaves litter until the next time the folder is opened. So only a positive answer that nobody is there counts as gone. Measured on the mac as an ordinary user, 2026-09-25: kill(1, 0) - launchd, root's - returns -1 with EPERM, and until #245 the import read that as gone and swept another account's live import; kill(0, 0) returns 0, because pid 0 means the caller's own process group; proc_name also fails with EPERM for another account's process; sysctl KERN_PROC_PID answers for ANY process - name, state and start time - and gives an empty answer for an id nobody holds. A zombie still answers the signal check, so the state is read from the table (measured: a finished child not yet collected answered kill 0 and the table said zombie).
liveness.whyTheStartTime: Every copy of Plantoir is called Plantoir, so the name check alone cannot tell a Plantoir that crashed from a different Plantoir that was later handed the same number - and since #245 a live lease REFUSES a second import rather than merely leaving litter, so a recycled number read as alive would block a retry until that unrelated process exits. The start time names the exact process. Windows' lease has no such line and its reader stops at the name; the mac writes the fourth line and Windows ignores it.
liveness.howToRunACase: signal is what the signal check answered: exists, noSuchProcess, notPermitted (EPERM) or otherError. table is what the process table answered: an object {name, zombie, start}, the string noSuchProcess, the string couldNotAsk, or null when the rule never asks it. lease is what the lease file records beyond its id: name (line 2) and start (line 4), null when absent. kind is the lease's kind when the case depends on it (only 'import' does), absent otherwise. A case with appliesOn ['mac'] is the mac's alone: Windows' reader treats a lease of fewer than two lines as stale and reads no import leases, so it has no such input. The rule is run against these answers directly, so a case needs no real process and runs as any user on any machine.

declining.rule: A build of a course from THIS program - Preview or Deploy in the window, the in-app assistant's rebuild or deploy, an outside assistant's rebuild or deploy (the mac's --mcp-stdio process) - is DECLINED when another live program holds a build, publish or preview lease on the same course. A publish set for later WAITS instead, and only for build and publish. Leases name the COURSE, not the section, so a build of Section 1 elsewhere declines Section 2 here too. This program's own leases are never in its way (the in-process rules decide that), a lease whose owner is gone is ignored (workLeases.liveness), and assist and import leases never decline a build.
declining.why: Two builds of one section clear and rewrite the same folder, so the loser serves a half-written site or publishes files the other has just deleted, and nothing fails loudly. Until #156 the mac's rules were in-process only, so an outside assistant (Claude Code or Codex reaching Plantoir --mcp-stdio), a publish set for later and the window could all build one course at once; Windows' plantoir-mcp and app already read each other's leases.
declining.whyAPreviewBlocks: Decided by the director on #156's plan review (2026-09-25, reversible, recorded on the issue), STRICTER than Windows, whose only blocking kind is build. Every build of a section first ends that section's serving preview (build_site.stop_preview_serving), so an outside assistant's rebuild or deploy would take down the page the teacher is reading - which the in-app assistant already refused to do - and an outside assistant can retry where a teacher reading a page cannot. A red case on Windows is the request.
declining.whyTheScheduledPublishWaits: Director's ruling (a), 2026-09-25, reversible. Going ahead anyway was REJECTED: two builds on one workspace is the fault being fixed. Standing down at once was REJECTED: a thirty-second build would cost a night's publish. So it waits - wall clock, so a Mac that sleeps does not pause the count - looking again every fifteen seconds for up to ten minutes, holding nothing while it waits; then takes its own build and publish leases and looks once more. Still busy at ten minutes, it stands down: deploys nothing, clears the job so it cannot recur, and leaves scheduledPublishStopped kind courseWasBusy for the section to show. It does not wait for a PREVIEW, because a preview left open overnight would otherwise cost the morning's publish; its build ends that preview, as it always has.
declining.takeThenCheck: Every door writes its own build lease FIRST and then looks, with nothing awaited in between, and then counts only a lease taken BEFORE its own build lease: an earlier moment (line 3), or the same moment and a lower process id. Two programs that each take a build and look at once therefore cannot BOTH go ahead - exactly one sees the other as earlier - and never both go ahead is the guarantee. The CLAIM is this program's build moment, not the earliest of its leases: a publish set for later does not wait for previews, so a window whose old preview lease predates such a publish's build must still decline its own Deploy, and an earliest-lease claim would let it go ahead (the review of #156 proposed that claim; the case above shows the two builds it allows). A Preview writes its build lease BEFORE its preview lease, so a Preview and an outside build that race cannot both back off either. What remains is one harmless shape: a Deploy pressed while this window already has a preview up, racing an outside build that lands between the two - both back off, nothing runs, and a retry works. The moments are compared as text, exact for the one fixed 28-character shape both apps write (UTC, seven fractional digits, of which the mac's DateFormatter fills three - millisecond resolution, so a same-moment tie is ordinary and goes to the lower pid); anything not in that shape counts as earlier. The window's Deploy takes its claim BEFORE it stops the teacher's preview, so its build lease is up for the whole of that stop: the stop (preview.sh --stop) ends builds as well as servers by working directory, and no other program may be told the course is free while it runs. The residual: a program that looks BEFORE it takes (Windows today, an older mac) can start in the instant between another's take and its own look; that is Windows' own shape and is recorded rather than closed.

whatIsSaid.window: wording.courseIsBeingBuiltElsewhere, in the window's Cannot Preview Yet or Cannot Deploy Yet alert - nothing has run, so the console has nothing to show
whatIsSaid.outsideAssistant: wording.courseIsBusy - it is talking to the program whose course is busy, and that sentence tells it to wait and ask again. publish_pages and undo_last_change still WRITE (Markdown never conflicts with a build) and leave the teacher's preview up; the note where the preview would have been refreshed is this sentence
whatIsSaid.scheduledPublish: nothing while it waits; scheduledPublishStopped.sentences.courseWasBusy if it stands down
whatIsSaid.trail: activityTrail.mustRecord 'build declined, course busy elsewhere' for every decline, and 'scheduled publish waited for the course' for a publish set for later that waited

rejected: ONE-WAY (the mac reading Windows-style leases but writing none, or writing but not reading) - Russell, 2026-09-25: 'yes, both ways'. Either half alone leaves one direction of the race open.
DOCUMENTING THE GAP instead of closing it - the fault is silent (a half-written site, nothing red), so a sentence in a manual would be the only defence and nobody reads it at the moment it matters.

CHECK-THEN-TAKE with no tiebreak (the plan's first shape, and Windows' today) - the window's Deploy awaits a preview stop between any early check and its own lease, so an outside build could start in that gap; the plan review measured the window, and the director ruled for take-then-check.

A SECTION in the lease name - Windows parses the kind as the third-last dot-separated part, so any extra part is a format change on both sides; course-level declines Section 2 for the length of a build of Section 1, and the sentence says which course.

A SWEEP of dead leases when a folder is opened - WorkLease's own design is no cleanup pass: a reader's liveness rule already ignores them, and the start time on line 4 settles the recycled-pid case the sweep was proposed for.

Greying the Deploy button while another program builds (Windows does) - a view cannot observe a file without a watcher, and declining at the press is the whole guarantee; a difference to know, not an obligation.
declining.howToRunACase: The asking program is course ICS3U with process id me.pid. me.claim is null for a look made BEFORE this program has taken its own build lease (every blocking lease counts), or {moment, pid} for the look made right after (only leases taken earlier count). others are the lease files in the folder: keep those whose course matches ICS3U without regard to case, whose pid is not me.pid, and whose alive is true (liveness is its own case list), then apply the rule for the asker - aBuild blocks on build, publish, preview; aScheduledPublish on build, publish. expect declined means the first blocking lease found stands in the way (for aScheduledPublish: it waits); allowed means nothing does. An entry with nameLine false is a lease file with no name on line 2: drop it too, for every kind but import (the liveness rule names an import lease itself); nameLine absent means the lease has one.

PAIR 1 of 2 - a Deploy pressed with a preview ALREADY up: window preview t1 < outside build t2 < window build t3. The window (claim t3) sees the outside build as earlier and declines

PAIR 2 of 2 - the outside program (claim t2) sees the window's older preview and declines too: BOTH back off. The harmless direction (nothing runs, a retry works) and kept rather than closed, because the one rule that closes it lets two builds run at once - see the next case

WHY the claim is this program's BUILD moment and not the earliest of its leases: a publish set for later took build and publish at t2 while the window's preview (t1) was up - it does not wait for previews - and the window's Deploy (build t3) must decline. Claimed from its preview (t1) instead, the window would read t2 as LATER and go ahead: two builds at once

a build lease with NO name line (or an empty one) is treated as gone, even with a live owner - neither app writes one, Windows' reader calls fewer than two lines stale, and judged on its id alone it could hold a course for the whole life of whatever was handed that id (#156; an import lease with no name is judged as Plantoir's instead - liveness)

folderPublishTarget.note: GitHub issue #227. Where a publish to a folder on this computer actually lands, and what a copy that did not finish is allowed to say. Run by scripts/test_deploy_folder_target.py against the real deploy.sh, started from a copy in a scratch working folder whose own name has a colon in it. @WF@ is replaced with that working folder as `/bin/pwd -P` spells it (the launcher's own spelling of it) and @ELSEWHERE@ with a writable scratch folder outside it, spelt the same way. Cases with `appliesOn: ["mac"]` (the per-case convention workLeases.liveness uses) use a colon, which NTFS does not allow in a folder name and which Windows reads as a drive letter ('a:b' is 'b' on drive A:), so they are the bash launcher's alone; the rest are portable in meaning, with Windows' separator. Windows' deploy.ps1 has no colon hole - robocopy has no remote syntax - but it does have the relative half; see documentation/07-deployment.md -> 'A relative folder, and a copy that did not finish'.
folderPublishTarget.rule: A relative --to-folder is taken from the working folder and made a full path before anything reads it, so nothing can take it for a remote computer or an option, and the folder the launcher names afterwards is one the app can open. A copy into the folder that did not finish - including one that finished only in part - is a failure: the launcher exits 1, says so in words the app lifts (app-rules.json -> failureExplanations), and prints no PUBLISHED_FOLDER= line, so nothing afterwards names the folder as published.

partialCopy.setUp: A full --to-folder whose section folder already holds a folder of stale pages that cannot be removed (its permissions forbid it), so the copy's --delete fails part way while every new page still lands.
partialCopy.why: Before: the copy's own exit status (23, 'finished in part') went into a pipe whose status was thrown away, so the launcher said Published and named the folder. A partial copy is a failure deliberately: the page left behind may be one the teacher took down. Not measured: network shares and iCloud Drive, where a copy can fail to set a file's attributes and report the same 'finished in part' - see documentation/07-deployment.md.
